Let the multitude perish then, which was borne in vaine, and let my grape be kept and my plant: for with great labor have I made it perfect.
Nevertheless if you will cease yet seven days moe (but you shall not fast in them.)
But go into a field of flowres, where no house is builded, and eat only the flowres of the field, Tast no flesh, drinke no wine, but eat flowres only.
And pray to the Highest continually, then will I come and talke with you.
So I went my way into the field which is called Ardath, like as he commanded me, and there I sate amongst the flowres, and did eat of the herbes of the field, and the food of the same satisfied me.
After seven days I sate upon the grasse, and my heart was vexed within me, like as before.
And I opened my mouth, and began to talke before the most High and said,
O Lord, you that show your selfe to us, you were showed to our fathers in the wildernesse, in a place where no man treads, in a barren place when they came out of Egypt.
And you spoke, saying, Hear me, O Yahsharala, and marke my words, you seed of Jacob.
For behold I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honored in it for ever.
But our fathers which received the law, kept it not, and obserued not your ordinances, and though the fruit of your law did not perish, neither could it, for it was yours:
Yet they that received it, perished, because they kept not the thing that was sowen in them.
And loe, it is a custome when the ground has received seed, or the Sea a ship, or any vessel, food or drinke, that, that being perished wherein it was sowen, or cast into,
That thing also which was sowen or cast therein, or received, does perish, and remains not with us: but with us it has not happened so.
For we that have received the law perish by sin, and our heart also which received it.
Notwithstanding the law perishes not, but remains in his force.

And when I spoke these things in my heart, I looked backe with mine eyes, and upon the right side I saw a woman, and behold, she mourned, and wept with a loud voyce, and was much grieved in heart, and her clothes were rent, and she had ashes upon her head.
Then let I my thoughts go that I was in, and turned me to her,
And said to her, Why do you weep? why art you so grieved in your minde?
And she said to me, Sir, let me alone, that I may bewaile my selfe, and adde to my sorow, for I am sore vexed in my minde, and brought very low.
And I said to her, What aileth you? Tell me.
She said to me, I your servant have bene barren, and had no childe, though I had an husband thirty yeres.
And those thirty years I did nothing else day and night, and every houre, but make my prayer to the highest.

After thirty years, Alahayam heard me your handmaid, looked upon my misery, considered my trouble, and gave me a son: and I was very glad of him, so was my husband also, and all my neighbours, and we gave great honor to the Almightie.
And I nourished him with great effort.
So when he grew up, and came to the time that he should have a wife, I made a feast.
And it so came to pass, that when my son was entred into his wedding chamber, he fell downe and died.
Then we all ouerthrew the lights, and all my neighbours rose up to comfort me, so I tooke my rest to the second day at night.
And it came to pass when they had all left off to comfort me, to the end I might be quiet: then rose I up by night and fled, and came here into this field, as you seest.
And I do now purpose not to returne into the city, but here to stay, and neither to eat nor drinke, but continually to mourne, and to fast vntil I die.
Then left I the meditations wherein I was, and spoke to her in anger, saying,
You foolish woman above all other, seest you not our mourning, and what happens to us?
How that Sion our mother is full of all heauinesse, and much humbled, mourning very sore?
And now seeing we all mourne, and are sad, for we are all in heauinesse, art you grieved for one son?
For aske the earth, and she shall tell you, that it is she, which ought to mourne, for the fall of so many that grow upon her.
For out of her came all at the first, and out of her shall all others come: and behold they walk almost all into destruction, and a multitude of them is vtterly rooted out.
Who then should make more mourning, then she that has lost so great a multitude, and not you which art sory but for one?
But if you sayest to me, My lamentation is not like the earths, because I have lost the fruit of my womb, which I brought foorth with paines, and bare with sorrowes.
But the earth not so: for the multitude present in it, according to the course of the earth, is gone, as it came.
Then say I to you, Like as you have brought foorth with labor: even so the earth also has given her fruit, namely man, ever sithence the beginning, to him that made her.
Now therefore keep your sorrow to your selfe, and beare with a good courage that which has befallen you.
For if you shall acknowledge the determination of Alahayam to be just, you shall both receive your son in time, and shall be commended amongst women.
Go your way then into the city, to your husband.
And she said to me, That will I not do: I will not go into the city, but here will I die.
So I proceeded to speak further to her, and said,
Do not so, but be counselled by me: for how many are the aduersities of Sion? Be comforted in regard of the sorow of Jerusalem.
For you seest that our Sanctuary is laid waste, our Altar broken downe, our Temple destroyed.

Our Psaltery is laid on the ground, our song is put to silence, our reioycing is at an end, the light of our candlesticke is put out, the Arke of our Couenant is spoiled, our holy things are defiled, and the Name that is called upon us, is almost prophaned: our children are put to shame, our priests are burnt, our Levites are gone into captiuitie, our virgines are defiled, and our wiues rauished, our righteous men caried away, our litle ones destroyed, our young men are brought in bondage, and our strong men are become weake.
And which is the greatest of all, the seale of Sion has now lost her honor: for she is deliuered into the hands of them that hate us.
And therefore shake off your great heauinesse, and put away the multitude of sorrowes, that the mighty may be mercifull to you again, and the highest shall give you rest, and ease from your labor.
And it came to pass while I was talking with her, behold her face upon a sudden shined exceedingly, and her countenance glistered, so that I was afraid of her, and mused what it might be.
And behold suddenly, she made a great cry very fearful: so that the earth shooke at the noise of the woman.

And I looked, and beholde, the woman appeared to me no more, but there was a city builded, and a large place showed it selfe from the foundations: then was I afraid, and cried with a lowd voice, and said,
Where is Uriel the Angel, who came to me at the first? for he has caused me to fall into many traunces, and mine end is turned into corruption, and my prayer to rebuke.
And as I was speaking these words, behold, he came to me, and looked upon me.
And loe, I lay as one that had bene dead, and mine understanding was taken from me, and he tooke me by the right hand, and comforted me, and set me upon my feet, and said to me,
What aileth you? and why art you so disquieted, and why is yours understanding troubled, and the thoughts of your heart?
And I said, because you have forsaken me, and yet I did according to your words, and I went into the field, and loe I have seene, and yet see, that I am not able to expresse.
And he said to me, Stand up manfully, and I will aduise you.
Then said I, Speak on, my lord in me, only forsake me not, lest I die frustrate of my hope.
For I have seene, that I knew not, and hear that I do not know.
Or, is my sense deceiued, or my soul in a dreame?
Now therfore, I beseech you, that you will show your servant of this vision.
He answered me then, and said, Hear me, and I shall enforme you, and tell you why you are afraid: for the highest will reueile many secret things to you.
He has seene that your way is right: for that you sorrow continually for your people, and makest great lamentation for Sion.
This therefore is the meaning of the vision which you lately sawest.
You sawest a woman mourning, and you beganst to comfort her:
But now seest you the likenesse of the woman no more, but there appeared to you a city builded.
And whereas she told you of the death of her son, this is the solution.
This woman whom you sawest, is Sion: and whereas she said to you (even she whom you seest as a city builded.)
Whereas I say, she said to you, that she has bene thirty yeres barren: those are the thirty years wherein there was no offering made in her.
But after thirty years, Solomon builded the city, and offered offrings: and then bare the barren a son.
And whereas she told you that she nourished him with labor: that was the dwelling in Hierusalem.
But whereas she said to you, That my son comming into his marriage chamber, happened to have a fall, and died, this was the destruction that came to Hierusalem.
And behold, you sawest her likenesse, and because she mourned for her son, you beganst to comfort her, and of these things which have chaunced, these are to be opened to you.
For now the most High seeth, that you are grieved vnfainedly, and suffer from your whole heart for her, so has he showed you the brightnes of her glory, and the comelinesse of her beautie.
And therfore I bad you remain in the field, where no house was builded.
For I knew that the Highest would show this to you.
Therefore I commanded you to go into the field, where no foundation of any building was.
For in the place wherein the Highest begins to show his city, ther can no mans building be able to stand.
And therfore fear not, let not your heart be afrighted, but go your way in, and see the beautie and greatnesse of the building, as much as your eyes be able to see:
And then shall you hear as much as your eares may comprehend.
For you are blessed above many other, and art called with the highest, and so are but few.
But to morrow at night you shall remain here.
And so shall the highest show you visions of the high things, which the most high will do to them, that dwel upon earth in the last days. So I slept that night and another, like as he commanded me.
Then saw I a dreame, and beholde, there came up from the Sea an Eagle, which had twelve feathered wings, and three heads.
And I saw, and behold, she spred her wings over all the earth, and all the windes of the ayre blewe on her, and were gathered together.
And I beheld, and out of her feathers there grewe other contrary feathers, and they became little feathers, and small.
But her heads were at rest: the head in the midst was greater then the other, yet rested it with the residue.
Moreouer I beheld, and loe, the Eagle flew with her feathers, and reigned upon earth, and over them that dwelt therein.
And I saw that all things under heaven were subiect to her, and no man spoke against her, no not one creature upon earth.
And I beheld, and loe, the Eagle rose upon her talents, and spoke to her feathers, saying,
Watch not all at once, sleepe every one in his own place, and watch by course.
But let the heads be preserued for the last.
And I beheld, and loe, the voice went not out of her heads, but from the midst of her body.
And I numbred her contrary feathers, and behold, there were eight of them.
And I looked, and behold, on the right side there arose one feather, and reigned over all the earth.
And so it was, that when it reigned, the ende of it came, and the place thereof appeared no more: so the next following stood up and reigned, and had a great time.
And it happened, that when it reigned, the end of it came also, like as the first, so that it appeared no more.
Then came there a voice to it, and said,
Hear, you that have borne rule over the earth so long: this I say to you, before you begin to appeare no more.
There shall none after you attaine to your time, neither to the halfe thereof.
Then arose the third, and reigned as the other before: and appeared no more also.
So went it with all the residue one after another, as that every one reigned, and then appeared no more.
Then I beheld, and loe, in processe of time, the feathers that folowed, stood up upon the right side, that they might rule also, and some of them ruled, but within a while they appeared no more:
For some of them were set up, but ruled not.
After this I looked, and behold, the twelve feathers appeared no more, nor the two little feathers:
And there was no more upon the Eagles body, but three heads that rested, and six little wings.
Then saw I also that two little feathers diuided themselues from the six, and remained under the head, that was upon the right side: for the four continued in their place.
And I beheld, and loe, the feathers that were under the wing, thought to set up themselues, and to have the rule.
And I beheld, and loe, there was one set up, but shortly it appeared no more.
And the second was sooner away then the first.
And I beheld, and loe, the two that remained, thought also in themselues to reigne.
And when they so thought, behold, there awaked one of the heads that were at rest, namely it that was in the midst, for that was greater then the two other heads.
And then I saw, that the two other heads were ioyned with it.
And behold, the head was turned with them that were with it, and did eat up the two feathers under the wing that would have reigned.

But this head put the whole earth in fear, and bare rule in it over all those that dwelt upon the earth, with much oppression, and it had the gouernance of the world more then all the wings that had been.
And after this I beheld, and loe the head that was in the midst, suddenly appeared no more, like as the wings.
But there remained the two heads, which also in like sort ruled upon the earth, and over those that dwelt therein.
And I beheld, and loe, the head upon the right side, deuoured it, that was upon the left side.
Then I heard a voyce, which said to me, Look before you, and consider the thing that you seest.
And I beheld, and loe, as it were a roaring Lyon, chased out of the wood: and I saw that he sent out a mans voyce to the Eagle, and said,
Hear you, I will talke with you, and the highest shall say to you,
Art not you it that remain of the four beasts, whom I made to raigne in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?

And the fourth came and ouercame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world with great fearefulnesse, and over the whole compasse of the earth with much wicked oppression, and so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit.
For the earth have you not iudged with truth.

For you have afflicted the meeke, you have hurt the peaceable, you have loued lyers, and destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit, and have cast downe the walles of such, as did you no harme.
Therefore is your wrongfull dealing come up to the Highest, and your pride to the Mighty.
The Highest also has looked upon the proud times, and behold, they are ended, and his abominations are fulfilled.
And therefore appeare no more you Eagle, nor your horrible wings, nor your wicked feathers, nor your malitious heads, nor your hurtfull clawes, nor all your vaine body:
That all the earth may be refreshed, and may returne, being deliuered from your violence, and that she may hope for the judgment, and mercy of him that made her.
And it came to pass whiles the Lyon spoke these words to the Eagle, I saw:
And behold, the head that remained, and the four wings appeared no more, and the two went to it, and set themselues up to raigne, and their kingdom was small and full of vprore.

And I saw, and behold, they appeared no more, and the whole body of the Eagle was burnt, so that the earth was in great fear: then awaked I out of the trouble and traunce of my minde, and from great fear, and said to my spirit,
Loe, this have you done to me, in that you search out the ways of the Highest.
Loe, yet am I weary in my mind, and very weake in my spirit: and litle strength is there in me; for the great fear, wherewith I was affrighted this night.
Therefore will I now beseech the Highest, that he will comfort me to the end.
And I said, Lord, that bear rule, If I have found grace before your sight, and if I am iustified with you, before many others, and if my prayer indeed be come up before your face,
Comfort me then, and show me your servant the interpretation, and plaine difference of this fearefull vision, that you maist perfectly comfort my soul.
For you have iudged me worthy, to show me the last times.
And he said to me, This is the interpretation of the vision.
The Eagle whom you sawest come up from the sea, is the kingdom which was seene, in the vision of your brother Daniel.
But it was not expounded to him, therefore now I declare it to you.
Behold, the days will come, that there shall rise up a kingdom upon earth, and it shall be feared above all the kingdoms that were before it.
In the same shall twelve kings reigne, one after another.
Whereof the second shall begin to reigne, and shall have more time then any of the twelve.
And this do the twelve wings signifie which you sawest.
As for the voice which you heard speak, and that you sawest not to go out from the heads, but from the mids of the body thereof, this is the interpretation:
That after the time of that kingdom, there shall arise great striuings, and it shall stand in perill of falling: nevertheless it shall not then fall, but shall be restored again to his beginning.
And whereas you sawest the eight small under feathers sticking to her wings, this is the interpretation:
That in him there shall arise eight kings, whose time shall be but small, and their years swift.
And two of them shall perish: the middle time approching, four shall be kept until their end begin to approch: but two shall be kept to the end.
And whereas you sawest three heads resting, this is the interpretation
In his last days shall the most High raise up three kingdoms, and renew many things therein, and they shall have the dominion of the earth,
And of those that dwell therein with much oppression, above all those that were before them: therefore are they called the heads of the Eagle.
For these are they that shall accomplish his wickednesse, and that shall finish his last end.
And whereas you sawest that the great head appeared no more, it signifies that one of them shall die upon his bed, and yet with paine.
For the two that remain, shall be slaine with the sword.
For the sword of the one shall deuoure the other: but at the last shall he fall through the sword himselfe.
And whereas you sawest two feathers under the wings passing over the head, that is on the right side:
It signifies that these are they whom the Highest has kept to their end: this is the small kingdom and full of trouble, as you sawest.
And the Lyon whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring, and speaking to the Eagle, and rebuking her for her vnrighteousnesse, with all the words which you have heard,
This is the Anointed which the Highest has kept for them, and for their wickednesse to the end: he shall reprooue them, and shall vpbraid them with their crueltie.
For he shall set them before him aliue in judgment, and shall rebuke them and correct them.

For the rest of my people shall he deliuer with mercy, those that have bin preserued upon my borders, and he shall make them ioyfull until the comming of the day of judgment, whereof I have spoken to you from the beginning.
This is the dreame that you sawest, and these are the interpretations.
You only have bene meete to know this secret of the Highest.
Therefore write all these things that you have seene, in a book, and hide them.
And teach them to the wise of the people, whose hearts you know may comprehend, and keep these seerets.
But wait you here your selfe yet seven days moe, that it may be showed you whatever it pleases the Highest to declare to you: And with that he went his way.

And it came to pass when all the people saw that the seven days were past, and I not come again into the city, they gathered them all together, from the least to the greatest, and came to me, and said,
What have we offended you? and what evil have we done against you, that you forsake us, and sit here in this place?
For of all the prophets you only art left us, as a cluster of the vintage, and as a candle in a darke place, and as a hauen or ship preserued from the tempest:
Are not the evils which are come to us, sufficient?
If you shall forsake us, how much better had it bene for us, if we also had bene burnt in the midst of Sion.
For we are not better then they that died there. And they wept with a loud voice: then answered I them, and said,
Be of good comfort, O Yahsharala, and be not heauy you house of Jacob.
For the Highest has you in remembrance, and the mighty has not forgotten you in temptation.
As for me, I have not forsaken you, neither am I departed from you: but am come into this place, to pray for the desolation of Sion, and that I might seeke mercy for the low estate of your Sanctuary.
And now go your way home every man, and after these days will I come to you.
So the people went their way into the city, like as I commanded them:
But I remained still in the field seven days, as the Angel commanded me, and did eat only in those days, of the flowers of the fielde, and ate the herbs as food.
And it came to pass after seven days, I dreamed a dreame by night.
And loe, there arose a winde from the sea that it mooued all the waues thereof.
And I beheld, and loe, that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled that were seene under him.
And whensoeuer the voyce went out of his mouth, all they burnt, that heard his voyce, like as the earth fails when it feels the fire.
And after this I beheld, and loe, there was gathered together a multitude of men out of number, from the four windes of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.
But I beheld, and loe, he had graued himselfe a great mountaine, and flew up upon it.
But I would have seene the region, or place, whereout the hill was grauen, and I could not.
And after this I beheld, and loe, all they which were gathered together to subdue him, were sore afraid, and yet durst fight.
And loe, as he saw the violence of the multitude that came, he neither lift up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war.
But only I saw that he sent out of his mouth, as it had bene a blast of fire, and out of his lippes a flaming breath, and out of his tongue he cast out sparkes and tempests,

And they were all mixt together; the blast of fire, the flaming breath, and the great tempest, and fel with violence upon the multitude, which was prepared to fight, and burnt them up every one, so that upon a sudden, of an innumerable multitude, nothing was to be perceiued, but only dust and smell of smoke: when I saw this, I was afraid.
Afterward saw I the same man come downe from the mountaine, and call to him an other peaceable multitude.

And there came much people to him, whereof some were glad, some were sory, some of them were bound, and other some brought of them that were offred: then was I sicke through great fear, and I awaked and said,
You have showed your servant wonders from the beginning, and have counted me worthy that you should receive my prayer:
Show me now yet the interpretation of this dreame.
For as I conceiue in mine understanding, woe to them that shall be left in those days; and much more woe to them that are not left behinde.
For they that were not left, were in heauinesse.
Now understand I the things that are layde up in the latter days, which shall happen to them, and to those that are left behinde.
Therefore are they come into great perils, and many necessities, like as these dreames declare.

Yet is it easier for him that is in danger, to come into these things, then to pass away as a cloud out of the world, and not to see the things that happen in the last days. And he answered to me, and said,
The interpretation of the vision shall I show you, and I will open to you, the thing that you have required.
Wheras you have spoken of them that are left behinde, this is the interpretation.
He that shall endure the perill in that time, has kept himselfe: they that be fallen into danger, are such as have workes, and faith towards the Almightie.
Know this therefore, that they which be left behinde, are more blessed then they that be dead.
This is the meaning of the vision: Whereas you sawest a man comming up from the midst of the Sea:
The same is he whom Alahayam the highest has kept a great season, which by his own selfe shall deliuer his creature: and he shall order them that are left behinde.
And whereas you sawest, that out of his mouth there came as a blast of winde, and fire, and storme:
And that he helde neither sword, nor any instrument of war, but that the rushing in of him destroyed the whole multitude that came to subdue him, this is the interpretation.
Behold, the days come, when the most high will begin to deliuer them that are upon the earth.
And he shall come to the astonishment of them that dwell on the earth.
And one shall vndertake to fight against another, one city against another, one place against another, one people against another, and one realme against another.
And the time shalbe, when these things shall come to pass, and the signes shall happen which I showed you before, and then shall my son be declared, whom you sawest as a man ascending.
And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land, leave the battaile they have one against another.
And an innumerable multitude shalbe gathered together, as you sawest them willing to come, and to overcome him by fighting.
But he shall stand upon the top of the mount Sion.
And Sion shall come and shall be showed to all men, being prepared and builded, like as you sawest the hill grauen without hands.
And this my son shall rebuke the wicked inuentions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest,

And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherwith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like to a flame: and he shall destroy them without labor, by the law which is like to fire.
And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him;

Those are the ten tribes, which were caried away prisoners out of their own land, in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria ledde away captive, and he caried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.
But they tooke this counsaile amongst themselues, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go foorth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt,
That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.
And they entred into Euphrates by the narrow passages of the Riuer.
For the most high then showed signes for them, and held still the flood, until they were passed over.
For through that country there was a great way to go; namely, of a year and a halfe: and the same region is called Arsareth.
Then dwelt they there until the latter time; and now when they shall begin to come,
The highest shall stay the springs of the streame again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.
But those that be left behinde of your people, are they that are found within my borders.
Now when he destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he shall defend his people that remain.
And then shall he shewe them great wonders.
Then said I, O Lord, that bear rule, show me this: Why have I seene the man comming up from the midst of the Sea?
And he said to me, Like as you can neither seeke out, nor know the things that are in the deepe of the sea: even so can no man upon earth see my son, or those that be with him, but in the day time.
This is the interpretation of the dreame which you sawest, and whereby you only art here lightened.
For you have forsaken your own way, and applied your diligence to my law, and sought it.
Your life have you ordered in wisdome, and have called understanding your mother.
And therefore have I showed you the treasures of the Highest: After other three days, I will speak other things to you, and declare to you mighty and wonderous things.
Then went I forth into the field giving praise and thanks greatly to the most High, because of his wonders which he did in time,
And because he governs the same, and such things as fall in their seasons, and there I sate three days.
And it came to pass, upon the third day I sate under an oke, and behold, there came a voyce out of a bush over against me, and said, Esdras, Esdras.
And I said, Here am I Lord, and I stood up upon my feet.
Then said he to me, In the bush I did manifestly reueale my selfe to Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt.
And I sent him, and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of Sinai, where I held him by me, a long season,
And told him many wonderous things, and showed him the secrets of the times, and the end, and commanded him, saying,
These words shall you declare, and these shall you hide.
And now I say to you,
That you lay up in your heart the signes that I have showed, and the dreames that you have seene, and the interpretations which you have heard:
For you shall be taken away from all, and from henceforth you shall remain with my son, and with such as be like you, until the times be ended.
For the world has lost his youth, and the times begin to waxe old.
For the world is diuided into twelve parts, and the ten parts of it are gone already, and halfe of a tenth part.
And there remains that which is after the halfe of the tenth part.
Now therefore set your house in order, and reproue your people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption.
Let go from you mortall thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weake nature,
And set aside the thoughts that are most heauy to you, and haste you to flie from these times.
For yet greater evils then those which you have seene happen, shall be done hereafter.
For look how much the world shall be weaker through age: so much the more shall evils increase upon them that dwell therein.
For the truth is fled farre away, and leasing is hard at hand: For now hastens the vision to come, which you have seene.
Then answered I before you, and said,

Behold, Lord, I will go as you have commanded me, and reprooue the people which are present, but they that shall be borne afterward, who shall admonish them? thus the world is set in darkenes, and they that dwell therein, are without light.
For your law is burnt, therefore no man knows the things that are done of you, or the works that shall begin.

But if I have found grace before you, send the holy Ghost into me, and I shall write all that has bene done in the world, since the beginning, which were written in your Lawe, that men may find your path, and that they which will live in the latter days, may live.
And he answered me, saying, Go your way, gather the people together, and say to them, that they seeke you not for forty days.
But look you prepare you many boxe trees, and take with you Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Eranus and Asiel, these five which are ready to write swiftly.
And come here, and I shall light a candle of understanding in your heart, which shall not be put out, until the things be performed which you shall beginne to write.
And when you have done, some things shall you publish, and some things shall you show secretly to the wise: to morrowe this houre shall you beginne to write.
Then went I foorth as he commanded, and gathered all the people together, and said,
Hear these words, O Yahsharala.
Our fathers at the beginning were strangers in Egypt, from whence they were deliuered:
And received the law of life which they kept not, which you also have transgressed after them.
Then was the land, even the land of Sion, parted among you by lot, but your fathers, and you your selues have done vnrighteousnesse, and have not kept the ways which the Highest commanded you.
And for as much as he is a righteous judge, he tooke from you in time, the thing that he had given you.
And now are you here, and your brethren amongst you.
Therefore if so be that you will subdue your own understanding, and reforme your hearts, you shall be kept aliue, and after death you shall obtaine mercy.
For after death, shall the judgment come, when we shall live again: and then shall the names of the righteous be manifest, and the workes of the ungodly shall be declared.
Let no man therefore come to me now, nor seeke after me these fourty days.
So I tooke the five men as he commanded me, and we went into the field, and remained there.
And the next day behold a voyce called me saying, Esdras, open your mouth and drinke that I give you to drinke.
Then opened I my mouth, and behold, he reached me a full cup, which was full as it were with water, but the colour of it was like fire.
And I tooke it, and dranke: and when I had drunke of it, my heart uttered understanding: and wisdom grew in my brest, for my spirit strengthened my memory.
And my mouth was opened and shut no more.

The highest gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote the wonderfull visions of the night, that were told, which they knew not: And they sate fourty days, and they wrote in the day, and at night they ate bread.
As for me I spoke in the day, and held not my tongue by night:
In fourty days they wrote two hundred and four books.
And it came to pass when the fourty days were fulfilled, that the Highest spoke, saying, The first that you have written, publish openly, that the worthy and vnworthy may read it.
But keep the seuenty last, that you may deliuer them only to such as be wise, among the people.
For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountains of wisdom, and the streame of knowledge.
And I did so.
Behold, do you speak in the eares of my people the words of prophesie, which I will put in your mouth, says the Lord.
And cause them to be written in paper: for they are faithfull and true.
Fear not the imaginations against you, let not the incredulity of them trouble you, that speak against you.
For all the vnfaithfull shall die in their vnfaithfulnesse.
Behold, says the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.
For wickednesse has exceedingly polluted the whole earth, and their hurtfull workes are fulfilled.
Therefore says the Lord,

I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickednesse, which they prophanely commit, neither will I suffer them in those things, in which they wickedly exercise themselues: behold, the innocent and righteous blood cryeth to me, and the souls of the just complaine continually.
And therefore says the Lord, I will surely auenge them, and receive to me, all the innocent blood from among them.
Beholde, my people is ledde as a flocke to the slaughter: I will not suffer them now to dwel in the land of Egypt.
But I will bring them with a mighty hand, and a stretched out arm, and smite Egypt with plagues as before, and will destroy al the land thereof.
Egypt shall mourne, and the foundation of it shall be smitten with the plague and punishment, that Alahayam shall bring upon it.
They that until the ground shall mourne: for their seedes shall faile, through the blasting, and haile, and with a fearefull constellation.
Woe to the world, and them that dwell therein.
For the sword and their destruction draws near, and one people shall stand up to fight against another, and swords in their hands.
For there shalbe sedition among men, and inuading one another, they shall not regard their kings, nor princes, and the course of their actions shall stand in their power.
A man shall desire to go into a city, and shall not be able.
For because of their pride, the cities shalbe troubled, the houses shalbe destroyed, and men shalbe afraid.
A man shall have no pity upon his neighbour, but shall destroy their houses with the sword, and spoile their goods, because of the lacke of bread, and for great tribulation.

Behold, says Alahayam, I will call together all the Kings of the earth to reuerence me, which are from the rising of the Sunne, from the South, from the East, and Libanus: to turne themselues one against another, and repay the things that they have done to them.
Like as they do yet this day to my chosen, so will I do also and recompense in their bosome, Thus says the Lord Alahayam;
My right hand shall not spare the sinners, and my sword shall not cease over them, that shed innocent blood upon earth.
The fire is gone foorth from his wrath, and has consumed the foundations of the earth, and the sinners like the straw that is kindled.
Wo to them that sin and keep not my commandments, says the Lord.
I will not spare them: go your way you children from the power, defile not my Sanctuary:
For the Lord knows all them that sin against him, and therefore delivers he them to death and destruction.
For now are the plagues come upon the whole earth, and you shall remain in them, for Alahayam shall not deliuer you, because you have sinned against him.
Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the East.
Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many charets, and the multitude of them shalbe caried as the winde upon earth, that all they which hear them, may fear and tremble.

Also the Carmanians raging in wrath, shall go forth as the wilde bores of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and ioyne battell with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.
And then shall the dragons have the vpper hand, remembering their nature, and if they shall turne themselues, conspiring together in great power to persecute them,
Then these shalbe troubled, and keep silence through their power, and shall flee.
And from the land of the Assyrians, shall the enemy besiege them, and consume some of them, and in their host shall be fear, and dread and strife among their kings.
Behold clouds from the East, and from the North, to the South, and they are very horrible to look upon; full of wrath and storme.
They shall smite one upon another, and they shall smite downe a great multitude of starres upon the earth, even their own starre; and blood shalbe from the sword to the belly.
And doung of men to the camels hough.
And there shalbe great fearefulnesse and trembling upon earth: and they that see the wrath, shall be afraid, and trembling shall come upon them.
And then shall there come great stormes, from the South, and from the North, and another part from the West.
And strong winds shall arise from the East, and shall open it, and the cloud which he raised up in wrath, and the starre stirred to cause fear toward the East and West winde, shalbe destroyed.

The great and mighty cloudes shall be lifted up full of wrath, and the starre, that they may make all the earth afraid, and them that dwel therein, and they shall power out over every high and eminent place, an horrible starre.
Fire and haile, and fleeing swords, and many waters, that all fields may be full, and all riuers with the abundance of great waters.
And they shall break downe the cities, and walls, mountaines and hils, trees of the wood, and grasse of the medowes, and their corne.
And they shall go stedfastly to Babylon, and make her afraid.
They shall come to her, and besiege her, the starre and all wrath shall they power out upon her, then shall the dust and smoke go up to the heaven: and all they that be about her, shall bewaile her.
And they that remain under her, shall do seruice to them that have put her in fear.
And you Asia that art partaker of the hope of Babylon, and art the glory of her person:

Woe be to you you wretch, because you have made your selfe like to her, and have deckt your daughters in whoredome, that they might please and glory in your louers, which have alway desired to commit whordome with you.
You have followed her, that is hated in all her works and inuentions: therefore sayth Alahayam,
I will send plagues upon you: widowhood, pouertie, famine, sword, and pestilence, to waste your houses with destruction and death.
And the glory of the power shall be dried up as floure, when the heate shall arise that is sent over you.
You shall be weakened as a poor woman with stripes, and as one chastised with woundes, so that the mighty and louers shall not be able to receive you.
Would I with iealousie have so proceeded against you, says the Lord,
If you had not alway slaine my chosen, exalting the stroke of your hands, and saying over their dead, when you were drunken,
Set foorth the beauty of your countenance.
The reward of your whoredome shall be in your bosome, therefore shall you receive recompense.
Like as you have done to my chosen, sayth the Lord; even so shall Alahayam do to you, and shall deliuer you into mischiefe.
Your children shall die of hunger, and you shall fall through the sword: your cities shalbe broken downe, and all yours shall perish with the sword in the field.
They that be in the mountaines shall die of hunger, and eat their own flesh, and drinke their own blood, for very hunger of bread, and thirst of water.
You, as vnhappy, shall come through the Sea, and receive plagues again.
And in the passage, they shall rush on the idle city, and shall destroy some portion of your land, and consume part of your glory, and shall returne to Babylon that was destroyed.
And you shall be cast downe by them, as stubble, and they shall be to you as fire,
And shall consume you and your cities, your land and your mountaines, all your woods and your fruitfull trees shall they burne up with fire.
Your children shall they cary away captive, and look what you have, they shall spoile it, and marre the beauty of your face.
Woe be to you, Babylon and Asia, woe be to you Egypt and Syria.
Gird up your selues with clothes of sacke and haire, bewaile your children, and be sory, for your destruction is at hand.
A sword is sent upon you, and who may turne it backe?
A fire is sent among you, and who may quench it?
Plagues are sent to you, and what is he that may driue them away?
May any man driue away a hungry Lion in the wood? or may any one quench the fire in stubble, when it has begun to burne?
May one turne again the arrow that is shot of a strong archer?
The mighty Lord sends the plagues, and who is he that can driue them away?
A fire shall go foorth from his wrath: and who is he that may quench it?
He shall cast lightnings, and who shall not fear? he shall thunder, and who shall not be afraid?
The Lord shall threaten, and who shall not be vtterly beaten to powder at his presence?

The earth quakes and the foundations thereof, the sea arises up with waues from the deepe, and the waues of it are troubled, and the fishes thereof also before the Lord, and before the glory of his power.
For strong is his right hand that bends the bow, his arrowes that he shoots are sharpe, and shall not misse when they begin to be shot into the ends of the world.
Behold, the plagues are sent, and shall not returne again, until they come upon the earth.
The fire is kindled, and shall not be put out, until it consume the foundation of the earth.
Like as an arrow which is shot of a mighty archer returns not backward: even so the plagues that shall be sent upon earth, shall not returne again.
Woe is me, woe is me, who will deliuer me in those days?

The beginning of sorrowes, and great mournings, the beginning of famine, and great death: the beginning of warres, and the powers shall stand in fear, the beginning of evils, what shall I do when these evils shall come?
Behold, famine, and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment.
But for all these things they shall not turne from their wickednes, nor be alway mindfull of the scourges.
Behold, victuals shall be so good cheape upon earth, that they shall think themselues to be in good case, and even then shall evils growe upon earth, sword, famine, and great confusion.
For many of them that dwell upon earth, shall perish of famine, and the other that escape the hunger, shall the sword destroy.
And the dead shall be cast out as doung, and there shalbe no man to comfort them, for the earth shall be wasted, and the cities shall be cast downe.
There shall be no man left to until the earth, and to sow it.
The trees shall give fruit, and who shall gather them?
The grapes shall ripe, and who shall treade them? for all places shall be desolate of men.
So that one man shall desire to see another, and to hear his voyce.
For of a city there shalbe ten left, and two of the field which shall hide themselues in the thicke groues, and in the clefts of rockes.
As in an orchard of oliues, upon every tree there are left three or four oliues:
Or, when as a vineyard is gathered, there are left some clusters of them that diligently seek through the vineyard:
Even so in those days there shalbe three or four left by them that search their houses with the sword.
And the earth shall be laid waste, and the fields thereof shall waxe old, and her ways and all her paths shall grow full of thornes, because no one shall travel through it.
The virgins shall mourne having no bridegromes, the women shall mourne having no husbands, their daughters shall mourne having no helpers.
In the warres shall their bridegromes be destroyed, and their husbands shall perish of famine.
Hear now these things, and understand them, you servants of the Lord.
Behold the word of the Lord, receive it, believe not the gods of whom the Lord spoke.
Behold, the plagues draw near, and are not slacke.

As when a woman with childe in the ninth month brings forth her son, within two or three houres of her birth great paines compasse her wombe, which paines, when the child comes forth, they slacke not a moment,
Even so shall not the plagues be slacke to come upon the earth, and the world shall mourne, and sorrowes shall come upon it on every side.
O my people, Hear my word: make you ready to the battell, and in those evils, be even as pilgrimes upon the earth.
He that sells let him be as he that fleeth away: and he that buyeth, as one that will loose.
He that trades in merchandise, as he that had no profit by it: and he that builds, as he that shall not dwell therein.
He that soweth, as if he should not reape: so also he that plants the vineyard, as he that shall not gather the grapes.
They that marry, as they that shall get no children: and they that marrie not, as the widowers.
And therefore they that labor, labor in vaine.
For strangers shall reape their fruits, and spoile their goods, ouerthrowe their houses; and take their children captives, for in captiuity and famine shall they get children.
And they that occupy their merchandize with robbery, the more they decke their citties, their houses, their possessions and their own persons:
The more will I be angry with them for their sin, says the Lord.
Like as an whore envies a right honest and vertuous woman:
So shall righteousness have iniquity, when she decks herselfe, and shall accuse her, to her face, when he comes that shall defend him that diligently searches out every sin upon earth.
And therfore be you not like therunto, nor to the workes thereof.
For yet a little iniquitie shall be taken away out of the earth, and righteousness shall reigne among you.
Let not the sinner say that he has not sinned: for Alahayam shall burne coales of fire upon his head, which says before the Lord Alahayam and his glory, I have not sinned.
Behold, the Lord knows all the workes of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts:
Which spoke but the word, let the earth be made, and it was made: let the heaven be made, and it was created.
In his word were the starres made, and he knows the number of them.
He searches the deepe, and the treasures thereof, he has measured the Sea, and what it contains.
He has shut the Sea in the midst of the waters, and with his word has he hanged the earth upon the waters.
He spreads out the heavens like a vault, upon the waters has he founded it.
In the desart has he made springs of water, and pooles upon the tops of the mountaines, that the floods might power downe from the high rockes to water the earth.
He made man, and put his heart in the midst of the body, and gave him breath, life, and understanding.
Yea and the spirit of Almighty Alahayam, which made all things, and searches out all hidden things in the secrets of the earth.
Surely he knows your inuentions, and what you thinke in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.
Therefore has the Lord exactly searched out all your workes, and he will put you all to shame.
And when your sins are brought foorth you shalbe ashamed before men, and your own sins shall be your accusers in that day.
What will you do? or how will you hide your sins before Alahayam and his Angels?

Behold, Alahayam himselfe is the judge, fear him: leave off from your sins, and forget your iniquities to medle no more with them for ever, so shall Alahayam do you lead forth, and deliuer you from all trouble.
For behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you, and they shall take away certaine of you, and feede you being idle with things offered to idoles.
And they that consent to them shall be had in derision, and in reproch, and troden under foote.
For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.
They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.
For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.
Then shall they be known who are my chosen, and they shall be tried, as the gold in the fire:
Hear, O you my beloued, says the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliuer you from the same.
Be you not afraid, neither doubt, for Alahayam is your guide,
And the guide of them who keep my commandments, and precepts, says the Lord Alahayam; Let not your sins weigh you downe, and let not your iniquities lift up themselues.

Woe be to them that are bound with their sins, and couered with their iniquities: like as a field is couered over with bushes, and the path thereof couered with thornes, that no man may trauell through.
It is left vndressed, and is cast into the fire, to be consumed therewith.
The Book of the words of Tobit, son of Tobiel, the son of Ananiel, the son of Aduel, the son of Gabael, of the seed of Asael, of the Tribe of Nephthali,
Who in the time of Enemessar king of the Assyrians, was led captive out of This be which is at the right hand of that city, which is called properly Nephthali in Galile above Aser.
I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the way of truth, and justice, and I did many alms deeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineveh into the land of the Assyrians.

And when I was in mine own country, in the land of Yahsharala, being but young, all the tribe of Nephthali my father, fell from the house of Jerusalem, which was chosen out of all the tribes of Yahsharala, that all the tribes should sacrifice there where the Temple of the habitation of the most High was consecrated, and built for all ages.
Now all the tribes which together revolted, and the house of my father Nephthali sacrificed to the heifer Baal.

But I alone went often to Jerusalem at the Feasts, as it was ordained to al the people of Yahsharala by an everlasting decree, having the first fruits, and tenths of encrease, with that which was first shorn, and them gave I at the Altar to the Priests the children of Aaron.
The first tenth part of al increase, I gave to the sons of Aaron, who ministered at Jerusalem: another tenth part I sold away, and went, and spent it every year at Jerusalem.
And the third, I gave to them to whom it was meet, as Debora my fathers mother had commanded me, because I was left an orphane by my father.
Furthermore when I was come to the age of a man, I married Anna of mine own kinred, and of her I begate Tobias.
And when we were caried away captives to Nineveh, all my brethren, and those that were of my kinred, did eat of the bread of the Gentiles.
But I kept my selfe from eating
Because I remembred Alahayam with all my heart.
And the most High gave me grace, and favor before Enemessar, so that I was his purueyour.
And I went into Media, and left in trust with Gabael, the brother of Gabrias at Rages a city of Media, ten talents of siluer.
Now when Enemessar was dead, Sennacherib his son reigned in his stead, whose estate was troubled, that I could not go into Media.
And in the time of Enemessar, I gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry,
And my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walles of Nineveh, I buried him.

And if the king Sennacherib had slaine any, when he was come, and fledde from Iudea, I buried them priuily, (for in his wrath he killed many) but the bodies were not found, when they were sought for of the king.
And when one of the Nineuites went, and complained of me to the king that I buried them, and hid my selfe: understanding that I was sought for to be put to death, I withdrew my selfe for fear.
Then all my goods were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, besides my wife Anna, and my son Tobias.

And there passed not five and fifty days before two of his sons killed him, and they fled into the mountaines of Ararath, and Sarchedonus his son reigned in his stead, who appointed over his fathers accounts, and over all his affaires, Achiacharus my brother Anaels son.

And Achiacharus entreating for me, I returned to Nineveh: now Achiacharus was Cup-bearer, and keeper of the Signet, and Steward, and ouerseer of the accounts: and Sarchedonus appointed him next to him: and he was my brothers son.

Now when I was come home again, and my wife Anna was restored to me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy Feast of the seven weekes, there was a good dinner prepared me, in the which I sate down to eat.
And when I saw abundance of food, I said to my son, Go and bring what poor man soeuer you shall find out of our brethren, who is mindfull of the Lord, and loe, I tarie for you.
But he came again and said, Father, one of our nation is strangled, and is cast out in the market place.
Then before I had tasted of any food, I start up and tooke him up into a room, until the going downe of the Sunne.
Then I returned and washed my selfe, and ate my food in heauinesse,
Remembering that prophesie of Amos, as he said; Your feasts shall be turned into mourning, and all your mirth into lamentation.
Therefore I wept: and after the going downe of the Sunne, I went and made a graue, and buried him.
But my neighbours mocked me, and said, This man is not yet afraide to be put to death for this matter, who fledde away, and yet loe, he buries the dead again.
The same night also I returned from the buriall, and slept by the wall of my court yard, being polluted, and my face was vncouered:

And I knewe not that there were Sparrowes in the wall, and mine eyes being open, the Sparrowes muted warme doung into mine eyes, and a whitenesse came in mine eyes, and I went to the Physicians, but they helped me not: moreouer Achiacharus did nourish me, until I went into Elymais.
And my wife Anna did take womens workes to do.
And when she had sent them home to the owners, they paid her wages, and gave her also besides a kid.
And when it was in mine house, and began to crie, I said to her, From whence is this kidde? is it not stollen? render it to the owners, for it is not lawfull to eat any thing that is stollen.

But she replyed upon me, It was given for a gift more then the wages: Howbeit I did not believe her, but bade her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replyed upon me, Where are yours alms, and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your workes are known.
Then I being grieved, did weepe, and in my sorrowe prayed, saying,
O Lord, you are just and all your workes, and all your ways are mercy and truth, and you judge truely and justly for ever.
Remember me, and look on me, punish me not for my sins and ignorances, and the sins of my fathers, who have sinned before you.
For they obeyed not your commandments, therefore you have deliuered us for a spoile, and to captiuitie, and to death, and for a prouerbe of reproch to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.
And now your iudgments are many and true: Deale with me according to my sins, and my fathers: because we have not kept your commandments, neither have walked in truth before you.

Now therefore deale with me as seems best to you, and command my spirit to be taken from me, that I may be dissolued, and become earth: for it is profitable for me to die, rather then to live, because I have heard false reproches, and have much sorow: command therfore that I may now be deliuered out of this distresse, and go into the everlasting place: turne not your face away from me.
It came to pass the same day, that in Ecbatane a city of Media, Sara the daughter of Raguel, was also reproched by her fathers maides,

Because that she had bin maried to seven husbands, whom Almodeus the evil spirit had killed, before they had lien with her. Do you not know, said they, that you have strangled your husbands? you have had already seven husbands, neither were you named after any of them.
Why do you beate us for them? If they be dead, go your ways after them, let us never see of you either son or daughter.

When she heard these things, she was very sorowful, so that she thought to have strangled her selfe, and she said, I am the only daughter of my father, and if I do this, it shall be a reproch to him, and I shall bring his old age with sorow to the graue.
Then she prayed toward the window, and said, Blessed art you, O Lord my Alahayam, and your holy and glorious Name is blessed, and honourable foreuer, let al your works praise you for ever.
And now, O Lord, I set mine eyes and my face toward you,
And say, take me out of the earth, that I may hear no more the reproch.
You know, Lord, that I am pure from all sin with man,

And that I never polluted my name, nor the name of my father in the land of my captiuitie: I am the only daughter of my father, neither has he any child to be his heire, neither any neere kinseman, nor any son of his aliue, to whome I may keep my selfe for a wife: my seven husbands are already dead, and why should I live? but if it please not you that I should die, command some regard to be had of me, and pity taken of me, that I hear no more reproch.
So the prayers of them both were heard before the Maiesty of the great Alahayam.

And Raphael was sent to heale them both, that is, to scale away the whitenesse of Tobits eyes, and to give Sara the daughter of Raguel, for a wife to Tobias the son of Tobit, and to bind Asmodeus the evil spirit, because she belongs to Tobias by right of inheritance. The selfe same time came Tobit home, and entred into his house, and Sara, the daughter of Raguel came downe from her vpper chamber.
In that day Tobit remembred the money, which he had committed to Gabael in Rages of Media,
And said with himselfe, I have wished for death, why do I not call for my son Tobias, that I may signifie to him of the money before I die.
And when he had called him, he said; My son, when I am dead, bury me, and despise not your mother, but honor her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and greiue her not.
Remember, my son, that she saw many dangers for you, when you were in her wombe, and when she is dead, bury her by me in one graue.

My son, be mindfull of the Lord our Alahayam all your days, and let not your will be set to sin, or to transgresse his Commandments: do vprightly all your life long, and follow not the ways of vnrighteousnesse.
For if you deale truely, your doings shall prosperously succeed to you, and to all them that live justly.
Give alms of your substance, and when you giuest alms, let not your eye be enuious, neither turne your face from any poor, and the face of Alahayam shall not be turned away from you.
If you have abundance, give alms accordingly: if you have but a litle, be not afraid to give according to that litle.
For you layest up a good treasure for your selfe against the day of necessitie.
Because that alms does deliuer from death, and suffers not to come into darknesse.
For alms is a good gift to all that give it, in the sight of the most High.

Beware of all whoredome, my son, and chiefely take a wife of the seed of your fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of your fathers tribe: for we are the children of the Prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaak, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all maried wiues of their own kinred, and were blessed in their children, and their seede shall inherite the land.

Now therefore my son, love your brethren, and despise not in your heart your brethren, the sons and daughters of your people, in not taking a wife of them: for in pride is destruction and much trouble, and in lewdnesse is decay, and great want: for lewdnesse is the mother of famine.

Let not the wages of any man, which has wrought for you, tary with you, but give him it out of hand: for if you serve Alahayam he will also repay you: be circumspect, my son, in all things you do, and be wise in all your conuersation.
Do that to no man which you hatest: drinke not wine to make you drunken; neither let drunkennesse go with you in your journey.
Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked, and according to your abundance give alms, and let not your eye be enuious, when you giuest alms.
Power out your bread on the buriall of the just, but give nothing to the wicked.
Aske counsel of all that are wise, and despise not any counsel that is profitable.

Blesse the Lord your Alahayam alway, and desire of him that your ways may be directed, and that all your pathes, and counsels may prosper: for every nation has not counsel, but the Lord himselfe gives all good things, and he humbles whom he will, as he will; now therefore my son, remember my commandments, neither let them be put out of your minde.
And now I signifie this to you, that I committed tenne talents to Gabael the son of Gabrias at Rages in Media.
And fear not my son, that we are made poor, for you have much wealth, if you fear Alahayam, and depart from all sin, and do that which is pleasing in his sight.
Tobias then answered and said, Father, I will do all things, which you have commanded me.
But how can I receive the money, seeing, I know him not?
Then he gave him the handwriting, and said to him, Seeke you a man which may go with you whiles I yet live, and I will give him wages, and go, and receive the money.
Therefore when he went to seeke a man, he found Raphael that was an Angell.
But he knew not; and he said to him, Canst you go with me to Rages? and do you know those places well?
To whom the Angel said, I will go with you, and I know the way well: for I have lodged with our brother Gabael.
Then Tobias said to him, Tary for me until I tell my father.

Then he said to him, Go and tary not; so he went in, and said to his father; Behold, I have found one, which will go with me. Then he said, Call him to me, that I may know of what tribe he is, and whether he be a trustie man to go with you.
So he called him, and he came in, and they saluted one another.
Then Tobit said to him, Brother, show me of what tribe and family you are.
To whom he said, Do you seeke for a tribe or family, or an hired man to go with your son? Then Tobit said to him, I would know, brother, your kinred, and name.
Then he said, I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of your brethren.

Then Tobit said, You are welcome brother, be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know your tribe, and your family, for you are my brother, of an honest and good stocke: for I know Ananias, and Ionathas sons of that great Samaias: as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the first borne, and the tenths of the fruits, and they were not seduced with the errour of our brethren: my brother, you are of a good stocke.
But tell me, what wages shall I give you? will you accept a drachma a day? and things necessary as to my own son?
Yea moreouer, if you returne safe, I will adde some thing to the wages.

So they were well pleased. Then said he to Tobias; Prepare your selfe for the journey, and Alahayam send you a good journey. And when his son had prepared all things for the journey, his father said; Go you with this man, and Alahayam which dwells in heaven prosper your journey, and the Angel of Alahayam keep you company. So they went foorth both, and the young mans dogge with them.
But Anna his mother wept, and said to Tobit, Why have you sent away our son? is he not the staffe of our hand, in going in and out before us?
Be not greedy (to adde) money to money: but let it be as refuse in respect of our childe.
For that which the Lord has given us to live with, does suffice us.
Then said Tobit to her, Take no care my sister he shall returne in safety, and your eyes shall see him.
For the good Angel will keep him company, and his journey shall be prosperous, and he shall returne safe.
Then she made an end of weeping.
And as they went on their journey, they came in the euening to the riuer Tigris, and they lodged there.
And when the young man went downe to wash himselfe, a fish leaped out of the riuer, and would have deuoured him.
Then the Angel said to him, Take the fish; and the young man layd hold of the fish, and drew it to land.
To whom the Angel said, Open the fish, and take the heart, and the liuer and the gall, and put them up safely.
So the young man did as the Angel commanded him, and when they had rosted the fish, they did eat it: then they both went on their way, until they drew neere to Ecbatane.
Then the young man saide to the Angel; Brother Azarias, to what use is the heart, and the liuer, and the gall of the fish?
And he said to him, Touching the heart and the liuer, if a deuil, or an evil spirit trouble any, we must make a smoke thereof before the man or the woman, and the party shalbe no more vexed.
As for the gall it is good to anoint a man that has whitenesse in his eyes, and he shalbe healed.
And when they were come neere to Rages;
The Angel said to the young man, Brother, to day we shall lodge with Raguel, who is your cousin; he also has one only daughter, named Sara, I will speak for her, that she may be given you for a wife.
For to you does the right of her appertaine, seeing you only art of her kinred.

And the maide is faire and wise, now therefore hear me, and I will speak to her father, and when we returne from Rages, we will celebrate the mariage: for I know that Raguel cannot marry her to another according to the Law of Moses, but he shalbe guiltie of death, because the right of inheritance does rather appertaine to you, then to any other.
Then the young man answered the Angel, I have heard, brother Azarias, that this maide has been given to seven men, who all died in the marriage chamber:

And now I am the only son of my father, and I am afraid, lest if I go in to her, I die, as the other before; for a wicked spirit loves her, which hurts no body, but those which come to her; therefore I also fear, lest I die, and bring my fathers and my mothers life (because of me) to the graue with sorrow, for they have no other son to bury them.

Then the Angel said to him, Do you not remember the precepts, which your father gave you, that you should marrie a wife of your own kindred? therefore hear me, O my brother, for she shall be given you to wife, and make you no reckoning of the evil spirit, for this same night shall she be given you in mariage.
And when you shall come into the mariage chamber, you shall take the ashes of perfume, and shall lay upon them, some of the heart, and liuer of the fish, and shall make a smoke with it.

And the deuill shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more: but when you shall come to her, rise up both of you, and pray to Alahayam, which is mercifull, who will have pity on you, and saue you: fear not, for she is appointed to you from the beginning; and you shall preserue her, and she shall go with you. Moreouer I suppose that she shall beare you children. Now when Tobias had heard these things, he loued her, and his heart was effectually ioyned to her.
And when they were come to Ecbatane, they came to the house of Raguel; and Sara met them: and after that they had saluted one another, she brought them into the house.
Then said Raguel to Edna his wife, How like is this young man to Tobit my cousin?
And Raguel asked them, From whence are you, brethren? To whom they said, We are of the sons of Nephthali, which are captives in Nineveh.
Then he said to them, Do you know Tobit our kinseman? And they said, We know him. Then said he, Is he in good health?
And they said, He is both aliue, and in good health: And Tobias said, He is my father.
Then Raguel leaped up, and kissed him, and wept,
And blessed him; and said to him, You are the son of an honest and good man: but when he had heard that Tobit was blinde, he was sorowfull, and wept.

And likewise Edna his wife, and Sara his daughter wept. Moreouer, they entertained them cheerefully, and after that they had killed a ramme of the flocke, they served plenty of meat on the table. Then said Tobias to Raphael, Brother Azarias, speak of those things, of which you did talke in the way, and let this businesse be dispatched.
So he communicated the matter with Raguel, and Raguel said to Tobias, Eat and drink, and make merry:
For it is meet that you should marry my daughter: nevertheless I will declare to you the truth.

I have given my daughter in mariage to seven men, who died that night they came in to her: nevertheless for the present be merry: But Tobias said, I will eat nothing here, until we agree and sweare one to another.
Raguel said, Then take her from hencefoorth according to the manner, for you are her cousin, and she is yours, and the mercifull Alahayam give you good successe in all things.

Then he called his daughter Sara, and she came to her father, and he tooke her by the hand, and gave her to be wife to Tobias, saying, Behold, take her after the Law of Moses, and leade her away to your father: And he blessed them,
And called Edna his wife, and tooke paper, and did write an instrument of couenants, and sealed it.
Then they began to eat.
After Raguel called his wife Edna, and said to her, Sister, prepare another chamber, and bring her in there.
Which when she had done as he had bidden her, she brought her there, and she wept, and she received the teares of her daughter, and said to her,
Be of good comfort, my daughter, the Lord of heaven and earth give you ioy for this your sorow: be of good comfort, my daughter.
And when they had supped, they brought Tobias in to her.
And as he went, he remembred the words of Raphael, and tooke the ashes of the perfumes, and put the heart, and the liuer of the fish thereupon, and made a smoke therewith.
The which smell, when the evil spirit had smelled, he fled into the outmost parts of Egypt, and the Angel bound him.
And after that they were both shut in together, Tobias rose out of the bed and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray, that Alahayam would have pity on us.
Then began Tobias to say, Blessed art you, O Alahayam of our fathers, and blessed is your holy and glorious Name for ever, let the heavens blesse you, and all your creatures.
You madest Adam, and gauest him Eue his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone, let us make to him an aide like to himselfe.
And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust, but vprightly: therefore mercifully ordeine, that we may become aged together.
And she said with him, Amen.
So they slept both that night, and Raguel arose, and went and made a graue
Saying, I fear lest he be dead.
But when Raguel was come into his house,
He said to his wife Edna, Send one of the maids, and let her see, whether he be aliue: if he be not, that we may bury him, and no man know it.
So the maid opened the doore and went in, and found them both asleepe,
And came forth, and told them, that he was aliue.

Then Raguel praised Alahayam, and said, O Alahayam, you are worthy to be praised with all pure and holy praise: therefore let your Saints praise you with all your creatures, and let all your Angels and your elect praise you for ever.
You are to be praised, for you have made me ioyfull, and that is not come to me, which I suspected: but you have dealt with us according to your great mercy.
You are to be praised, because you have had mercy of two, that were the only begotten children of their fathers, grant them mercy, O Lord, and finish their life in health, with ioy and mercy.
Then Raguel bade his servants to fill the graue.
And he kept the wedding feast fourteene days.
For before the days of the mariage were finished, Raguel had said to him by an othe, that he should not depart, until the fourteene days of the mariage were expired,
And then he should take the halfe of his goods, and go in safetie to his father, and should have the rest when I and my wife be dead.
Then Tobias called Raphael, and said to him,
Brother Azarias, Take with you a servant, and two camels, and go to Rages of Media to Gabael, and bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding.
For Raguel has sworne that I shall not depart.
But my father counts the days, and if I tarie long, he will be very sorie.
So Raphael went out and lodged with Gabael, and gave him the handwriting, who brought forth bags, which were sealed up, and gave them to him.
And earely in the morning they went forth both together, and came to the wedding, and Tobias blessed his wife.
Nowe Tobit his father counted every day, and when the days of the journey were expired, and they came not:
Then Tobit said, Are they detained? or is Gabael dead? and there is no man to give him the money?
Therefore he was very sory.
Then his wife said to him, My son is dead, seeing he stays long, and she began to bewaile him, and said,
Now I care for nothing, my son, since I have let you go, the light of mine eyes.
To whom Tobit said, Hold your peace, take no care; for he is safe.

But she said, Hold your peace, and deceiue me not: my son is dead, and she went out every day into the way which they went, and ate no food during the day, and ceased not whole nights, to bewaile her son Tobias, until the fourteen days of the wedding were expired, which Raguel had sworne, that he should spend there: Then Tobias said to Raguel, Let me go, for my father, and my mother look no more to see me.
But his father in law said to him, Tary with me, and I will send to your father, and they shall declare to him, how things go with you.
But Tobias said, No: but let me go to my father.
Then Raguel arose and gave him Sara his wife, and halfe his goods, servants, and cattell, and money.
And he blessed them, and sent them away, saying, The Alahayam of heaven give you a prosperous journey, my children.

And he said to his daughter, Honor your father and your mother in law, which are now your parents, that I may hear good report of you: and he kissed her. Edna also said to Tobias, The Lord of heaven restore you, my dear brother, and grant that I may see your children of my daughter Sara before I die, that I may rejoice before the Lord: behold, I commit my daughter to you of speciall trust, therefore do not entreate her evil.
After these things Tobias went his way, praising Alahayam that he had given him a prosperous journey, and blessed Raguel, and Edna his wife, and went on his way until they drew neere to Nineveh.
Then Raphael said to Tobias, You know brother, how you did leave your father.
Let us haste before your wife, and prepare the house.
And take in your hand the gall of the fish: so they went their way, and the dog went after them.
Now Anna sate looking about towards the way for her son.
And when she espied him comming, she said to his father, Behold, your son comes, and the man that went with him.
Then said Raphael, I know, Tobias, that your father will open his eyes.
Therefore annoint you his eies with the gall, and being pricked therewith he shall rub, and the whitenesse shall fall away, and he shall see you.
Then Anna ran forth, and fell upon the necke of her son, and said to him, seeing I have seene you my son, from henceforth, I am content to die, and they wept both.
Tobit also went forth toward the doore, and stumbled: but his son ran to him,
And tooke hold of his father, and he strake of the gall on his fathers eyes, saying, Be of good hope, my father.
And when his eyes began to smart, he rubbed them.
And the whitenesse pilled away from the corners of his eyes, and when he saw his son, he fell upon his necke.
And he wept, and said, Blessed art you, O Alahayam, and blessed is your Name for ever, and blessed are all your holy Angels:
For you have scourged, and have taken pity on me: for behold, I see my son Tobias. And his son went in reioycing, and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.
Then Tobit went out to meete his daughter in law at the gate of Niniue, reioycing and praysing Alahayam: and they which saw him go, marueiled because he had received his sight.

But Tobit gave thankes before them: because Alahayam had mercy on him. And when he came neere to Sara his daughter in Law, he blessed her, saying, You are welcome daughter: Alahayam be blessed which has brought you to us, and blessed be your father and your mother; And there was ioy amongst all his brethren which were at Nineveh.
And Achiacharus, and Nasbas his brothers son came.
And Tobias wedding was kept seven days with great ioy.
Then Tobit called his son Tobias, and said to him, My son, see that the man have his wages, which went with you, and you must give him more.
And Tobias said to him, O father, it is no harme to me to give him halfe of those things which I have brought.
For he has brought me again to you in safety, and made whole my wife, and brought me the money, and likewise healed you.
Then the old man said: It is due to him.
So he called the Angell, and he said to him, Take halfe of all that you have brought, and go away in safety.

Then he tooke them both apart, and said to them, Blesse Alahayam, praise him, and magnifie him, and praise him for the things which he has done to you in the sight of all that live. It is good to praise Alahayam and exalt his name, and honorably to show forth the works of Alahayam, therfore be not slacke to praise him.
It is good to keep close the secret of a King, but it is honorable to reueale the works of Alahayam: do that which is good, and no evil shall touch you.
Prayer is good with fasting, and alms and righteousness: a little with righteousnes is better then much with vnrighteousnesse: it is better to give alms then to lay up gold.
For alms does deliuer from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms, and righteousness, shall be filled with life.
But they that sin are enemies to their own life.
