For by these means he thought, finding us destitute of friends to have translated the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians.
But we find that the Jews, whom this wicked wretch has delivered to utter destruction, are no evildoers, but live by most just laws:
And that they be children of the most high and most mighty, living Alahayam, who has ordered the kingdom both unto us and to our progenitors in the most excellent manner.
Therefore you shall do well not to put in execution the letters sent unto you by Aman the son of Amadatha.
For he that was the worker of these things, is hanged at the gates of Susa with all his family: Alahayam, who ruleth all things, speedily rendering vengeance to him according to his deserts.
Therefore you shall publish the copy of this letter in all places, that the Jews may freely live after their own laws.
And you shall aid them, that even the same day, being the thirteenth day of the twelfth month Adar, they may be avenged on them, who in the time of their affliction shall set upon them.
For Almighty Alahayam has turned to joy unto them the day, wherein the chosen people should have perished.
You shall therefore among your solemn feasts keep it an high day with all feasting:
That both now and hereafter there may be safety to us and the well affected Persians; but to those which do conspire against us a memorial of destruction.

Therefore every city and country whatsoever, which shall not do according to these things, shall be destroyed without mercy with fire and sword, and shall be made not only unpassable for men, but also most hateful to wild beasts and fowls for ever.
Love righteousness, you that be judges of the earth: thinke of the Lord with a good (heart) and in simplicitie of heart seeke him.
For he will be found of them that tempt him not: and shows himselfe to such as do not distrust him.
For froward thoughts separate from Alahayam: and his power when it is tryed, reproves the vnwise.
For into a malitious soul wisdom shall not enter: nor dwell in the body that is subiect to sin.
For the holy spirit of discipline will flie deceit, and remoue from thoughts that are without understanding: and will not abide when vnrighteousnesse comes in.
For wisdom is a louing spirit: and will not acquite a blasphemour of his words: for Alahayam is witnesse of his reines, and a true beholder of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
For the spirit of the Lord fills the world: and that which contains all things has knowledge of the voice.
Therefore he that speaks unrighteous things, cannot be hid: neither shall vengeance, when it punishes. pass by him.
For inquisition shall be made into the counsels of the ungodly: and the sound of his words, shall come to the Lord, for the manifestation of his wicked deeds.
For the eare of iealousie hears al things: and the noise of murmurings is not hid.
Therefore beware of murmuring, which is vnprofitable, and refraine your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belies, slays the soul.
Seeke not death in the errour of your life: and pull not upon your selues destruction, with the workes of your hands.
For Alahayam made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.
For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthfull: and there is no poyson of destruction in them: nor the kingdom of death upon the earth.
For righteousness is immortall.

But ungodly men with their workes, and words called it to them: for when they thought to have it their friend, they consumed to nought, and made a couenant with it, because they are worthy to take part with it.

For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselues, but not aright: Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedie: neither was there any man known to have returned from the graue.
For we are borne at all aduenture: and we shalbe heereafter as though we had never bene: for the breath in our nostrils is as smoke, and a litle sparke in the mouing of our heart.
Which being extinguished, our body shall be turned into ashes, and our spirit shall vanish as the soft aire:

And our name shalbe forgotten in time, and no man shall have our works in remembrance, and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud: and shall be dispersed as a mist that is driuen away with the beames of the Sunne, and overcome with the heat thereof.
For our time is a very shadow that passes away: and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man comes again.
Come on therefore, let us enioy the good things that are present: and let us speedily use the creatures like as in youth.
Let us fill our selues with costly wine, and ointments: and let no flower of the Spring pass by us.
Let us crowne our selues with Rose buds, before they be withered.
Let none of us go without his part of our voluptuousnesse: let us leave tokens of our ioyfulnesse in every place: for this is our portion, and our lot is this.
Let us oppresse the poor righteous man, let us not spare the widow, nor reuerence the ancient gray haires of the aged.
Let our strength be the Lawe of justice: for that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth.

Therefore let us lye in wait for the righteous: because he is not for our turne, and he is cleane contrary to our doings: he rebukes us with our offending the Law, and objects to our infamy the transgressings of our education.
He professes to have the knowledge of Alahayam: and he calls himselfe the childe of the Lord.
He was made to reprooue our thoughts.
He is grieuous to us even to beholde: for his life is not like other mens, his waies are of another fashion.
We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstains from our ways as from filthinesse: he pronounces the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Alahayam is his father.
Let us see if his words be true: and let us proue what shall happen in the end of him.
For if the just man be the son of Alahayam, he will helpe him, and deliuer him from the hand of his enemies.
Let us examine him with despitefulnesse and torrture, that we may know his meekenesse, and prooue his patience.
Let us condemne him with a shamefull death: for by his own saying, he shall be respected.
Such things they did imagine, and were deceiued: for their own wickednesse has blinded them.
As for the mysteries of Alahayam, they knew them not: neither hoped they for the wages of righteousness: nor discerned a reward for blamelesse souls.
For Alahayam created man to be immortall, and made him to be an image of his own eternitie.
Nevertheless through enuie of the deuill came death into the world: and they that do holde of his side do find it.
But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Alahayam, and there shall no torment touch them.
In the sight of the vnwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery,
And their going from us to be vtter destruction: but they are in peace.
For though they be punished in the sight of men: yet is their hope full of immortalitie.
And having bene a little chastised, they shalbe greatly rewarded: for Alahayam proued them, and found them worthy for himselfe.
As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.
And in the time of their visitation, they shall shine and runne to and fro, like sparkes among the stubble.
They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Lord shall raigne for ever.
They that put their trust in him, shall understand the truth: and such as be faithfull in love, shall abide with him: for grace and mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect.
But the ungodly shalbe punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken the Lord.
For who so despises wisdom, and nurture, he is miserable, and their hope is vaine, their labours vnfruitfull, and their works vnprofitable.
Their wiues are foolish, and their children wicked.
Their of-spring is cursed: therefore blessed is the barren that is vndefiled, which has not known the sinfull bed: she shall have fruit in the visitation of souls.

And blessed is the Eunuch which with his hands has wrought no iniquitie: nor imagined wicked things against Alahayam: for to him shall be given the speciall gift of faith, and an inheritance in the Temple of the Lord more acceptable to his minde.
For glorious is the fruit of good labours: and the root of wisedom shall never fall away.
As for the children of adulterers, they shall not come to their perfection, and the seed of an unrighteous bed shall be rooted out.
For though they live long, yet shall they be nothing regarded: and their last age shall be without honor.
Or if they die quickly, they have no hope, neither comfort in the day of triall.
For horrible is the end of the unrighteous generation.
Better it is to have no children, and to have vertue: for the memoriall thereof is immortal: because it is known with Alahayam and with men.
When it is present, men take example at it, and when it is gone they desire it: it wears a crown, and triumphs for ever, having gotten the victorie, striuing for vndefiled rewards.
But the multiplying brood of the ungodly shall not thriue, nor take deepe rooting from bastard slips, nor lay any fast foundation.
For though they flourish in branches for a time: yet standing not fast, they shall be shaken with the winde: and through the force of windes they shall be rooted out.
The vnperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit vnprofitable, not ripe to eat: yea meet for nothing.
For children begotten of vnlawfull beds, are witnesses of wickednes against their parents in their triall.
But though the righteous be preuented with death: yet shall he be in rest.
For honourable age is not that which stands in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years.
But wisdom is the gray haire to men, and an vnspotted life is old age.
He pleased Alahayam, and was beloued of him: so that living amongst sinners, he was translated.
Yea, speedily was he taken away, lest that wickednes should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.
For the bewitching of naughtines does obscure things that are honest: and the wandring of concupiscence, does vndermine the simple mind.
He being made perfect in a short time, fulfilled a long time.
For his soul pleased the Lord: therefore hasted he to take him away, from among the wicked.
This the people saw, and understood it not: neither laid they up this in their mindes, That his grace and mercy is with his Saints, and that he has respect to his chosen.
Thus the righteous that is dead, shall condemne the ungodly, which are living, and youth that is soone perfected, the many years and old age of the unrighteous.
For they shall see the end of the wise, and shall not understand what Alahayam in his counsel has decreed of him, and to what end the Lord has set him in safetie.
They shall see him and despise him, but Alahayam shall laugh them to scorne, and they shall hereafter be a vile carkeis, and a reproch among the dead for evermore.

For he shall rend them, and cast them downe headlong, that they shalbe speechles: and he shall shake them from the foundation: and they shall be vtterly laid waste, and be in sorow: and their memoriall shall perish.
And when they cast up the accounts of their sins, they shall come with fear: and their own iniquities shall conuince them to their face.
Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldnesse, before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.
When they see it, they shalbe troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangenesse of his saluation, so farre beyond all that they looked for.
And they repenting, and groning for anguish of spirit, shall say within themselues, This was he whom we had sometimes in derision, and a prouerbe of reproch.
We fooles accounted his life madnes, and his end to be without honor.
How is he numbred among the children of Alahayam, and his lot is among the Saints?
Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined to us, and the Sunne of righteousness rose not upon us.
We wearied ourselues in the way of wickednesse, and destruction: yea, we have gone through deserts, where there lay no way: but as for the way of the Lord, we have not known it.
What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?
All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a Poste that hasted by.
And as a ship that passes over the waues of the water, which when it is gone by, the trace thereof cannot be found: neither the path way of the keele in the waues.

Or as when a bird has flowen thorow the aire, there is no token of her way to be found, but the light aire being beaten with the stroke of her wings, and parted with the violent noise and motion of them, is passed thorow, and therin afterwards no signe where she went, is to be found.
Or like as when an arrow is shot at a marke, it parts the aire, which immediatly comes together again: so that a man cannot know where it went thorow:
Even so we in like manner, assoone as we were borne, began to draw to our end, and had no signe of vertue to show: but were consumed in our own wickednesse.

For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blowen away with the wind, like a thinne froth that is driuen away with the storme: like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passes away as the remembrance of a guest that tarries but a day.
But the righteous live for evermore, their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.
Therfore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crowne from the Lords hande: for with his right hand shall he couer them, and with his arm shall he protect them.
He shall take to him his ielousie for complete armour, and make the creature his weapon for the reuenge of his enemies.
He shall put on righteousness as a brestplate, and true judgment in stead of an helmet.
He shall take holinesse for an inuincible shield.
His seuere wrath shall he sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the vnwise.
Then shall the right-aiming thunder bolts go abroad, and from the cloudes, as from a well-drawen bow, shall they flie to the marke.
And hailestones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stonebow, and the water of the Sea shall rage against them, and the floods shall cruelly drowne them.
Yea a mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a storme shall blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay were the whole earth, and ill dealing shall ouerthrow the thrones of the mighty.
Hear therefore, O you kings, and understand, learne you that be judges of the ends of the earth.
Give eare you that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations.
For power is given you of the Lord, and soueraigntie from the Highest, who shall try your workes; and search out your counsels.
Because being Ministers of his kingdom, you have not iudged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of Alahayam,
Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharpe judgment shall be to them that be in high places.
For mercy will soone pardon the mean: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.
For he which is Lord over all, shall fear no mans person: neither shall he stand in awe of any mans greatnesse: for he has made the small and great, and careth for all alike.
But a sore triall shall come upon the mighty.
Unto you therefore, O kings, do I speak, that you may learne wisdom, and not fall away.
For they that keep holinesse holily, shall be iudged holy: and they that have learned such things, shall find what to answer.
Therefore set your affection upon my words, desire them, and you shall be instructed.
Wisdom is glorious and never fadeth away: yea she is easily seene of them that love her, and found of such as seeke her.
She anticipates them that desire her, in making herselfe first known to them.
Whoso seeks her earely, shall have no great effort: for he shall find her sitting at his doores.
To thinke therefore upon her is perfection of wisdom: and who so watches for her, shall quickly be without care.
For she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, shows herselfe fauourably to them in the ways, and meets them in every thought.
For the very true beginning of her, is the desire of discipline, and the care of discipline is love:
And love is the keeping of her lawes; and the giving heed to her lawes, is the assurance of incorruption.
And incorruption makes us neere to Alahayam.
Therefore the desire of wisdom brings to a kingdom.
If your delight be then in thrones and scepters, O you kings of the people, honor wisdom that you may raigne for evermore.

As for wisdom what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seeke her out from the beginning of her natiuity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth.
Neither will I go with consuming enuy: for such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom.
But the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the world: and a wise king is the vpholding of the people.
Receive therefore instruction thorough my words, and it shall do you good.
I my selfe also am a mortall man, like to all, and the ofspring of him that was first made of the earth,
And in my mothers wombe was fashioned to be flesh in the time of tenne moneths being compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure that came with sleepe.
And when I was borne, I drew in the common aire, and fell upon the earth which is of like nature, and the first voice which I uttered, was crying as all others do.
I was nursed in swadling clothes, and that with cares.
For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth.
For all men have one entrance to life, and the like going out.
Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Alahayam, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
I preferred her before scepters, and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
Neither compared I to her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and siluer shalbe counted as clay before her.
I loued her above health and beautie, and chose to have her in stead of light: for the light that comes from her never goes out.
All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands.
And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goes before them: and I knew not that she was the mother of them.
I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.
For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use, become the friends of Alahayam: being commended for the gifts that come from learning.
Alahayam has granted me to speak as I would, and to conceiue as is meet for the things that are given me: because it is he that leads to wisdom, and directs the wise.
For in his hand are both we and our words: all wisdom also and knowledge of workemanship.
For he has given me certaine knowledge of the things that are, namely to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements:
The beginning, ending, and midst of the times: the alterations of the turning of the Sunne, and the change of seasons:
The circuits of yeres, and the positions of starres:
The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wilde beasts: the violence of windes, and the reasonings of men: the diuersities of plants, and the vertues of rootes:
And all such things as are either secret or manifest: them I know.

For wisdom which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtile, liuely, cleare, vndefiled, plaine, not subiect to hurt, louing the thing that is good, quicke, which cannot be letted, ready to do good:
Kinde to man, stedfast, sure, free from care, having all power, ouerseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtile spirits.
For wisdom is more moouing then any motion: she passes and goes through all things by reason of her purenesse.
For she is the breath of the power of Alahayam, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no vndefiled thing fall into her.
For she is the brightnesse of the everlasting light: the vnspotted mirrour of the power of Alahayam, and the Image of his goodness.
And being but one she can do all things: and remayning in her selfe, she makes all things new: and in all ages entring into holy souls, she makes them friends of Alahayam, and Prophets.
For Alahayam loves none but him, that dwells with wisdom.
For she is more beautiful then the Sunne, and above all the order of starres, being compared with the light, she is found before it.
For after this comes night: but vice shall not preuaile against wisdome.
Wisdome reaches from one ende to another mightily: and sweetly does she order all things.
I loued her and sought her out, from my youth I dedesired to make her my spouse, and I was a louer of her beautie.
In that she is conuersant with Alahayam, she magnifies her nobilitie: yea, the Lord of all things himselfe loued her.
For she is priuy to the mysteries of the knowledge of Alahayam, and a louer of his workes.
If riches be a possession to be desired in this life: what is richer then wisdom that works all things?
And if prudence worke; who of all that are, is a more cunning workeman then she?
And if a man love righteousness, her labours are vertues: for she teaches temperance and prudence: justice and fortitude, which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in their life.

If a man desire much experience: she knows things of old, and conjectures aright what is to come: she knows the subtilties of speaches, and can expound darke sentences: she foresees signes and wonders, and the euents of seasons and times.
Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with me, knowing that she would be a counsellour of good things, and a comfort in cares and griefe.
For her sake I shall have estimation among the multitude, and honor with the Elders, though I be young.
I shall be found of a quicke conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of great men.
When I hold my tongue they shall bide my leisure, and when I speak they shall give good eare to me: if I talke much, they shall lay their handes upon their mouth.
Moreouer, by the meanes of her, I shall obtaine immortalitie, and leave behind me an everlasting memoriall to them that come after me.
I shall set the people in order, and the nations shalbe subiect to me.
Horrible tyrants shall be afraide when they do but hear of me, I shall be found good among the multitude, and valiant in war.
After I am come into mine house, I will repose my selfe with her: for her conuersation has no bitternes, and to live with her, has no sorrow, but mirth and ioy.
Now when I considered these things in my selfe, and pondered them in mine heart, how that to be allyed to wisdom, is immortalitie,

And great pleasure it is to have her friendship, and in the workes of her hands are infinite riches, and in the exercise of conference with her, prudence: and in talking with her a good report: I went about seeking how to take her to me.
For I was a wittie child, and had a good spirit.
Yea rather being good, I came into a body vndefiled.

Nevertheless when I perceiued that I could not otherwise obtaine her, except Alahayam gave her me (and that was a point of wisdome also to know whose gift she was) I prayed to the Lord, and besought him, and with my whole heart I said:
O Alahayam of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who have made all things with your word,
And ordained man through your wisdom, that he should have dominion over the creatures, which you have made,
And order the world according to equitie and righteousness, and execute judgment with an vpright heart:
Give me wisdom that sits by your Throne, and reiect me not from among your children:
For I your servant and son of your handmaide, am a feeble person, and of a short time, and too young for the understanding of judgment and lawes.
For though a man be never so perfect among the children of men, yet if your wisdom be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded.
You have chosen me to be a king of your people, and a Judge of your sons and daughters:
You have commanded me to build a Temple upon your holy mount, and an Altar in the city wherein you dwell, a resemblance of the holy Tabernacle which you have prepared from the beginning:
And wisdom was with you: which knows your workes, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your Commandments.
O send her out of your holy heavens, and from the Throne of your glory, that being present she may labor with me, that I may know what is pleasing to you.
For she knows and understands all things, and she shall leade me soberly in my doings, and preserue me in her power.
So shall my workes be acceptable, and then shall I judge your people righteously, and be worthy to sit in my fathers seate.
For what man is he that can know the counsel of Alahayam? or who can thinke what the will of the Lord is?
For the thoughts of mortall men are miserable, and our deuices are but vncertaine.
For the corruptible body presses downe the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weighs downe the minde that museth upon many things.
And hardly do we gesse aright at things that are upon earth, and with labor do we find the things that are before us: but the things that are in heaven, who has searched out?
And your counsel who has known, except you give wisdom, and send your holy spirit from above?
For so the ways of them which liued on the earth were reformed, and men were taught the things that are pleasing to you, and were saued through wisdom.
She preserued the first formed father of the world that was created alone, and brought him out of his fall,
And gave him power to rule all things.
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherwith he murdered his brother.
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, Wisdom again preserued it, and directed the course of the righteous, in a piece of wood, of small value.

Moreouer, the nations in their wicked conspiracie being confounded, she found out the righteous, and preserued him blamelesse to Alahayam, and kept him strong against his tender compassion towards his son.
When the ungodly perished, she deliuered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell downe upon the five cities.

Of whose wickednesse even to this day the waste land that smokes, is a testimonie, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripenesse: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an vnbeleeuing soul.

For regarding not wisdom, they gate not only this hurt, that they knew not the things which were good: but also left behind them to the world a memoriall of their foolishnes: so that in the things wherein they offended, they could not so much as be hid.
But Wisdom deliuered from paine those that attended upon her.

When the righteous fled from his brothers wrath, she guided him in right paths: showed him the kingdom of Alahayam: and gave him knowledge of holy things, made him rich in his trauailes, and multiplied the fruit of his labours.
In the couetousnesse of such as oppressed him, she stood by him, and made him rich.
She defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those that lay in wait, and in a sore conflict she gave him the victory, that he might know that godlinesse is stronger then all.
When the righteous was solde, she forsooke him not, but deliuered him from sin: she went downe with him into the pit,

And left him not in bonds until she brought him the scepter of the kingdom and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she showed them to be liers, and gave them perpetuall glory.
She deliuered the righteous people, and blamelesse seed from the nation that oppressed them.
She entred into the soul of the servant of the Lord, and withstood dreadfull kings in wonders and signes,
Rendred to the righteous a reward of their labours, guided them in a marueilous way, and was to them for a couer by day, and a light of starres in the night season:
Brought them through the red sea, and led them thorow much water.
But she drowned their enemies, and cast them up out of the bottome of the deepe.
Therefore the righteous spoiled the ungodly, and praised your holy Name, O Lord, and magnified with one accord your hand that fought for them.
For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumbe, and made the tongues of them that cannot speak, eloquent.
She prospered their works in the hand of the holy Prophet.
They went thorough the wildernesse that was not inhabited, and pitched tents in places where there lay no way.
They stood against their enemies, and were auenged of their aduersaries.
When they were thirsty they called upon you, and water was given them out of the flinty rocke, and their thirst was quenched out of the hard stone.
For by what things their enemies were punished, by the same they in their neede were benefited.
For in stead of a fountaine of a perpetuall running riuer, troubled with foule blood,
For a manifest reproofe of that commandment, whereby the infants were slaine, you gauest to them abundance of water by a meanes which they hoped not for,
Declaring by that thirst then, how you had punished their aduersaries.
For when they were tryed, albeit but in mercy chastised, they knew how the ungodly were iudged in wrath and tormented thirsting in another manner then the Just.
For these you did admonish, and trie as a father: but the other as a seuere king you did condemne and punish.
Whether they were absent, or present, they were vexed alike.
For a double griefe came upon them, and a groaning for the remembrance of things past.
For when they heard by their own punishments the other to be benefited, they had some feeling of the Lord.
For whom they reiected with scorne when he was long before throwen out at the casting forth of the infants, him in the end, when they saw what came to pass, they admired.

But for the foolish deuises of their wickednesse, wherewith being deceiued, they worshipped serpents voyd of reason, and vile beasts: you did send a multitude of vnreasonable beasts upon them for vengeance,
That they might know that wherewithall a man sins, by the same also shall he be punished.
For your Almighty hand that made the world of matter without forme, wanted not meanes to send among them a multitude of Beares, or fierce Lyons,
Or vnknowen wild beasts full of rage newly created, breathing out either a fiery vapour, or filthy sents of scattered smoake, or shooting horrible sparkles out of their eyes:
Whereof not only the harme might dispatch them at once: but also the terrible sight vtterly destroy them.

Yea and without these might they have fallen downe with one blast, being persecuted of vengeance, and scattered abroad thorough the breath of your power, but you have ordered all things in measure, and number, and weight.
For you can show your great strength at all times when you will, and who may withstand the power of your arm?
For the whole world before you is as a litle graine of the ballance, yea as a drop of the morning dew that falls downe upon the earth.
But you have mercy upon all: for you can do all things, and wink at the sins of men: because they should amend.
For you louest all the things that are, and abhor nothing which you have made: for never would you have made any thing, if you had hated it.
And how could any thing have endured if it had not been your will? or been preserued, if not called by you?
But you spare all: for they are yours, O Lord, you louer of souls.
For your vncorruptible spirit is in all things.
Therefore chasten you them by little, and little, that offend, and warn them by putting them in remembrance, wherin they have offended, that leaving their wickednesse they may believe on you O Lord.
For it was your will to destroy by the handes of our fathers, both those old inhabitants of your holy land,
Whom you hatedst for doing most odious workes of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices;
And also those mercilesse murderers of children, and deuourers of mans flesh, and the feasts of blood;
With their Priests out of the midst of their idolatrous crew, and the parents that killed with their own hands, souls destitute of helpe:
That the land which you esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy colonie of Gods children.
Nevertheless, even those you sparedst as men, and did send waspes forerunners of your hoste, to destroy them by little and little.
Not that you were vnable to bring the ungodly under the hand of the righteous in battell, or to destroy them at once with cruel beastes, or with one rough word:

But executing your iudgements upon them by little and little, you gauest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughtie generation, and that their malice, was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.
For it was a cursed seed, from the beginning, neither did you for fear of any man give them pardon for those things wherein they sinned.

For who shall say, What have you done? or who shall withstand your judgment, or who shall accuse you for the nations that perish whom you have made? or who shall come to stand against you, to be reuenged for the unrighteous men?
For neither is there any Alahayam but you, that careth for all, to whom you might show that your judgment is not vnright.
Neither shall king or tyrant be able to set his face against you, for any whom you have punished.
For so much then as you are righteous your selfe, you order all things righteously: thinking it not agreeable with your power to condemne him who has not deserved to be punished.
For your power is the beginning of righteousness, and because you are the Lord of all, it makes you to be gracious to all.
For when men will not believe, that you are of a full power, you show your strength, and among them that know it, you makest their boldnesse manifest.
But you, mastering your power, judge with equitie, and order us with great favor: for you may use power when you will.
But by such workes have you taught your people, that the just man should be mercifull, and have made your children to be of a good hope, that you giuest repentance for sins.
For if you did punish the enemies of your children, and the condemned to death with such deliberation, giving them time and place, wherby they might be deliuered from their malice.
With how great circumspection did you judge your own sons, to whose fathers you have sworne, and made couenants of good promises?

Therefore whereas you do chasten us, you scourge our enemies a thousand times more, to the intent that when we judge, we should carefully thinke of your goodness, and when we our selues are iudged, we should look for mercy.
Therefore, whereas men have liued dissolutely and vnrighteously, you have tormented them with their own abominations.
For they went astray very farre in the ways of errour, and held them for gods (which even amongst the beasts of their enemies were despised) being deceiued as children of no understanding.
Therefore to them, as to children without the use of reason, you did send a judgment to mocke them.
But they that would not be refourmed by that correction wherein he dallied with them, shall feele a judgment worthy of Alahayam.

For look, for what things they grudged when they were punished, (that is) for them whom they thought to be gods, being punished in them; when they saw it, they acknowledged him to be the true Alahayam, whome before they denyed to know: and therefore came extreme damnation upon them.

Surely vaine are all men by nature, who are ignorant of Alahayam, and could not out of the good things that are seene, know him that is: neither by considering the workes, did they acknowledge the worke-master;
But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift aire, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven to be the gods which gouerne the world:
With whose beautie, if they being delighted, tooke them to be gods: let them know how much better the Lord of them is; for the first Author of beautie has created them.
But if they were astonished at their power and vertue, let them understand by them, how much mightier he is that made them.
For by the greatnesse and beautie of the creatures, proportionably the Maker of them is seene.
But yet for this they are the lesse to be blamed: for they peraduenture erre seeking Alahayam, and desirous to find him.
For being conuersant in his workes, they search him diligently, and believe their sight: because the things are beautifull that are seene.
Howbeit, neither are they to be pardoned.
For if they were able to know so much, that they could aime at the world; how did they not sooner find out the Lord thereof?

But miserable are they, and in dead things is their hope, who called them gods which are the workes of mens hands, golde and siluer, to shewe arte in, and resemblances of beasts, or a stone good for nothing, the worke of an ancient hand.

Now a carpenter that fells timber, after he has sawen downe a tree meet for the purpose, and taken off all the barke skilfully round about, and has wrought it handsomely, and made a vessell thereof fit for the seruice of mans life:
And after spending the refuse of his worke to prepare his food, has filled himselfe:

And taking the very refuse among those which served to no use (being a crooked piece of wood, and ful of knots) has carued it diligently when he had nothing else to do, and formed it by the skill of his understanding, and fashioned it to the image of a man:
Or made it like some vile beast, laying it over with vermilion, and with paint, colouring it red, and couering every spot therein:
And when he had made a conuenient room for it, set it in a wall, and made it fast with yron:
For he prouided for it, that it might not fall: knowing that it was vnable to helpe it selfe, (for it is an image and has neede of helpe:)
Then makes he prayer for his goods, for his wife and children, and is not ashamed to speak to that which has no life.

For health, he calls upon that which is weake: for life, prays to that which is dead: for aide, humbly beseeches that which has least meanes to helpe: and for a good journey, he asketh of that which cannot set a foot forward:
And for gaining and getting, and for good successe of his hands, asketh abilitie to do, of him that is most vnable to do any thing.
Again, one preparing himselfe to saile, and about to pass through the raging waues, calls upon a piece of wood more rotten then the vesell that carries him.
For verely desire of gaine deuised that, and the workeman built it by his skill:
But your providence, O Father, governs it: for you have made a way in the Sea, and a safe path in the waues:
Showing that you can saue from all danger: yea though a man went to Sea without arte.
Nevertheless you would not that the works of your wisdom should be idle, and therefore do men commit their liues to a small piece of wood, and passing the rough sea in a weake vessell, are saued.
For in the old time also when the proud gyants perished, the hope of the world gouerned by your hand, escaped in a weake vessell, and left to all ages a seed of generation.
For blessed is the wood, whereby righteousness comes.
But that which is made with hands, is cursed, aswell it, as he that made it: he, because he made it, and it, because being corruptible it was called Alahayam.
For the ungodly and his vngodlines are both alike hatefull to Alahayam.
For that which is made, shall be punished together with him that made it.

Therfore even upon the idoles of the Gentiles shall there be a visitation: because in the creature of Alahayam they are become an abomination and stumbling blocks to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the vnwise.
For the deuising of idoles was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the inuention of them the corruption of life.
For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever.
For by the vaine glory of men they entred into the world, and therefore shall they come shortly to an end.

For a father afflicted with vntimely mourning, when he has made an image of his childe soone taken away, now honored him as a god, which was then a dead man, and deliuered to those that were under him, ceremonies and sacrifices.
Thus in processe of time an ungodly custome growen strong, was kept as a law, and grauen images were worshipped by the commandments of kings,

Whom men could not honor in presence, because they dwelt farre off, they tooke the counterfeit of his visage from farre, and made an expresse image of a king whom they honored, to the end that by this their forwardnes, they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present.
Also the singular diligence of the artificer did helpe to set forward the ignorant to more superstition.
For he peraduenture willing to please one in authoritie, forced all his skill to make the resemblance of the best fashion.
And so the multitude allured by the grace of the worke, tooke him now for a god, which a litle before was but honored as a man.
And this was an occasion to deceiue the world: for men seruing either calamitie or tyrannie, did ascribe to stones, and stockes, the incommunicable Name.
Moreouer this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of Alahayam, but whereas they liued in the great war of ignorance, those so great plagues called they peace.
For while they slew their children in sacrifices, or used secret ceremonies, or made reuellings of strange rites
They kept neither liues nor mariages any longer vndefiled: but either one slew another traiterously, or grieved him by adulterie:
So that there reigned in all men without exception, blood, manslaughter, theft, and dissimulation, corruption, vnfaithfulnesse, tumults, periurie,
Disquieting of good men, forgetfulnesse of good turnes, defiling of souls, changing of kinde, disorder in mariages, adulterie, and shameles vncleannesse.
For the worshipping of idoles not to be named, is the beginning, the cause, and the end of all evil.
For either they are mad when they be merry, or prophesie lies, or live vniustly, or else lightly forsweare themselues.
For insomuch as their trust is in idoles which have no life, though they sweare falsly, yet they look not to be hurt.
Howbeit for both causes shall they be justly punished: both because they thought not well of Alahayam, giving heed to idols, and also vniustly swore in deceit, despising holinesse.
For it is not the power of them by whom they sweare: but it is the just vengeance of sinners, that punishes always the offence of the ungodly.
But you O Alahayam, art gracious and true: long suffering, and in mercy ordering all things.
For if we sin we are yours, knowing your power: but we will not sin, knowing that we are counted yours.
For to do you know is perfect righteousness: yea to know your power is the roote of immortality.
For neither did the mischieuous inuention of men deceiue us: nor an image spotted with diverse colours, the painters fruitlesse labor.
The sight wherof entices fooles to lust after it, and so they desire the forme of a dead image that has no breath.
Both they that make them, they that desire them, and they that worship them, are louers of evil things, and are worthy to have such things to trust upon.

For the potter tempering soft earth fashions, every vessell with much labor for our seruice: yea of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serve for cleane vses: and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the potter himselfe is the judge.

And employing his labours lewdly, he makes a vaine Alahayam of the same clay, even he which a little before was made of earth himselfe, and within a little while after returns to the same out of the which he was taken: when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.

Notwithstanding his care is, not that he shall have much labor, nor that his life is short: but strives to excel goldsmiths, and siluersmiths, and endeavors to do like the workers in brasse, and counts it his glory to make counterfeit things.
His heart is ashes, his hope is more vile then earth, and his life of lesse value then clay:
Forasmuch as he knew not his maker, and him that inspired into him an actiue soul, and breathed in a living spirit.
But they counted our life a pastime, and our time here a market for gaine: for, say they, we must be getting every way, though it be by evil meanes.
For this man that of earthly matter makes brickle vessels, and grauen images, knows himselfe to offend above all others.
And all the enemies of your people, that hold them in subiection are most foolish and are more miserable then very babes.

For they counted all the idoles of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor eares to hear, nor fingers of hands to handle, and as for their feete they are slow to go.
For man made them, and he that borrowed his own spirit fashioned them, but no man can make a god like to himselfe.
For being mortall he works a dead thing with wicked hands: for he himselfe is better then the things which he worships: whereas he liued once, but they never.
Yea they worshipped those beasts also that are most hatefull: for being compared together, some are worse then others.
Neither are they beautifull, so much, as to be desired in respect of beasts, but they went without the praise of Alahayam and his blessing.
Therefore by the like were they punished worthily, and by the multitude of beasts tormented.
In stead of which punishment, dealing graciously with your own people you preparedst for them food of a strange taste: even quailes to stirre up their appetite:

To the end that they desiring food might for the ougly sight of the beasts sent among them, loath even that which they must needs desire: but these suffering penury for a short space, might be made partakers of a strange taste.
For it was requisite, that upon them excercising tyranny should come penury which they could not auoyde: but to these it should only be showed how their enemies were tormented.
For when the horrible fiercenesse of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, your wrath endured not for ever.
But they were troubled for a smal season that they might be admonished, having a signe of saluation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of your Law.
For he that turned himselfe towards it, was not saued by the thing that he saw: but by you that art the sauiour of all.
And in this you madest your enemies confesse, that it is you who deliver from all evil:
For them the bitings of grassehoppers and flies killed, neither was there found any remedy for their life: for they were worthy to be punished by such.
But your sons, not the very teeth of venemous dragons ouercame: for your mercy was ever by them, and healed them.
For they were pricked, that they should remember your words, and were quickly saued, that not falling into deep forgetfulnesse, they might be continually mindefull of your goodness.
For it was neither herbe, nor mollifying plaister that restored them to health: but your word, O Lord, which heals all things.
For you have power of life and death: you lead to the gates of hell, and bring up again.
A man indeed kills through his malice: and the spirit when it is gone foorth returns not; neither the soul received up, comes again.
But it is not possible to escape your hand.

For the ungodly that denied to do you know, were scourged by the strength of your arm: with strange raines, hailes, and showers were they persecuted, that they could not auoyd, and through fire were they consumed.
For, which is most to be wondered at, the fire had more force in the water that quenches all things: for the world fights for the righteous.

For sometimes the flame was mitigated, that it might not burne up the beasts that were sent against the ungodly: but themselues might see and perceiue that they were persecuted with the judgment of Alahayam.
And at another time it burns even in the midst of water, above the power of fire, that it might destroy the fruits of an vniust land.
In stead whereof you fed your own people, with Angels food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labor, able to content every mans delight, and agreeing to every taste.
For your sustenance declared your sweetnesse to your children, and seruing to the appetite of the eater tempered it selfe to every mans liking.
But snow and yce endured the fire and melted not, that they might know that fire burning the haile, and sparkling in the raine, did destroy the fruits of the enemies.
But this again did even forget his own strength, that the righteous might be nourished.
For the creature that serves you who art the maker, increases his strength against the unrighteous for their punishment, and abates his strength for the benefit of such as put their trust in you.
Therefore even then was it altered into all fashions, and was obedient to your grace that nourishes all things, according to the desire of them that had need:
That your children, O Lord, whom you louest, might know that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word which preserves them that put their trust in you.
For that which was not destroied of the fire, being warmed with a litle Sunne beame, soone melted away,
That it might be known, that we must preuent the Sunne, to give you thanks, and at the day-spring pray to you.
For the hope of the vnfaithfull, shall melt away as the Winters hoarefrost, and shall runne away as vnprofitable water.
For great are your Iudgements, and cannot be expressed: therefore vnnourtured souls have erred.

For when unrighteous men thought to oppresse the holy nation: they being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkenesse, and fettered with the bondes of a long night, lay exiled from the eternall providence.
For while they supposed to lie hid in their secret sins, they were scattered under a darke vaile of forgetfulnesse, being horribly astonished, and troubled with (strange) apparitions.
For neither might the corner that helde them keep them from fear: but noises (as of waters) falling downe, sounded about them, and sadde visions appeared to them with heauie countenances.
No power of the fire might give them light: neither could the bright flames of the starres endure to lighten that horrible night.
Only there appeared to them a fire kindled of it selfe, very dreadfull: for being much terrified, they thought the things which they saw to be worse then the sight they saw not.
As for the illusions of arte Magicke, they were put downe, and their vaunting in wisdom was reprooued with disgrace.
For they that promised to driue away terrours, and troubles from a sicke soul, were sicke themselues of fear worthy to be laughed at.
For though no terrible thing did fear them: yet being skared with beasts that passed by, and hissing of serpents,
They died for fear, denying that they saw the ayre, which could of no side be auoided.
For wickednesse condemned by her own witnesse, is very timorous, and being pressed with conscience, always forecasts grieuous things.
For fear is nothing else, but a betraying of the succours which reason offers.
And the expectation from within being lesse, counts the ignorance more then the cause which brings the torment.
But they sleeping the same sleepe that night which was indeed intolerable, and which came upon them out of the bottomes of ineuitable hell:
Were partly vexed with monstrous apparitions, and partly fainted, their heart failing them: for a suddaine fear and not looked for, came upon them.
So then, whoever there fell downe, was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without yron barres.

For whether he were husbandman, or shepheard, or a labourer in the field, he was ouertaken, and endured that necessitie, which could not be auoided: for they were all bound with one chaine of darkenesse.
Whether it were a whistling winde, or a melodious noise of birdes among the spreading branches, or a pleasing fall of water running violently:

Or a terrible sound of stones cast downe, or a running that could not be seene of skipping beasts, or a roaring voice of most sauage wilde beasts, or a rebounding Eccho from the hollow mountaines: these things made them to swoone for fear.
For the whole world shined with cleare light, and none were hindered in their labor.
Over them only was spread an heauie night, an image of that darkenesse which should afterwards receive them: but yet were they to themselues more grieuous then the darkenesse.
Nevertheless, your Saints had a very great light, whose voice they hearing and not seeing their shape, because they also had not suffered the same things, they counted them happy.
But for that they did not hurt them now, of whom they had been wronged before, they thanked them, and besought them pardon, for that they had been enemies.
In stead whereof you gauest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the vnknowen journey, and an harmelesse Sunne to entertaine them honourably.
For they were worthy to be depriued of light, and imprisoned in darknesse, who had kept your sons shut up, by whom the vncorrupt light of the law was to be given to the world.

And when they had determined to slay the babes of the Saints, one child being cast forth, and saued: to reproue them, you took away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them altogether in a mighty water.
Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing to what oathes they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheere.
So of your people was accepted both the saluation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.
For wherewith you did punish our aduersaries, by the same you did glorifie us whom you had called.

For the righteous children of good men did sacrifice secretly, and with one consent made a holy lawe, that the Saints should be alike partakers of the same good and evil, the fathers now singing out the songs of praise.
But on the other side there sounded an ill-according crie of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was caried abroad for children that were bewailed.
The master and the seruaunt were punished after one manner, and like as the king, so suffered the common person.
So they altogether had innumerable dead with one kind of death, neither were the living sufficient to burie them: for in one moment the noblest ofspring of them was destroyed.
For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments, upon the destruction of the first borne, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of Alahayam.
For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course,
Your almighty word leapt downe from heaven, out of your royall throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction,
And brought your vnfained commandment as a sharpe sword, and standing up filled all things with death, and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.
Then suddenly visions of horrible dreames troubled them sore, and terrours came upon them vnlooked for.
And one throwen here, another there halfe dead, showed the cause of his death.
For the dreames that troubled them, did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.
Yea, the tasting of death touched the righteous also, and there was a destruction of the multitude in the wildernes: but the wrath endured not long.

For then the blamelesse man made haste, and stood foorth to defend them, and bringing the shield of his proper ministerie, even prayer and the propitiation of incense, set himselfe against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was your servant.
So he ouercame the destroyer, not with strength of body, nor force of arms, but with a word subdued he him that punished, alleaging the oathes and couenants made with the fathers.
For when the dead were now fallen downe by heaps one upon another, standing between, he staied the wrath, and parted the way to the living.
For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rowes of the stones was the glory of the fathers grauen, and your maiestie upon the diademe of his head.
To these the destroyer gave place, and was afraid of them: for it was enough that they only tasted of the wrath.
As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy to the end: for he knew before what they would do;
Howe that having given them leave to depart, and sent them hastily away, they would repent and pursue them.
For while they were yet mourning, and making lamentation at the graues of the dead, they added another foolish deuice, and pursued them as fugitiues, whom they had entreated to be gone.

For the destiny, whereof they were worthy, drew them to this end, and made them forget the things that had already happened, that they might fulfill the punishment which was wanting to their torments,
And that your people might pass a wonderfull way: but they might find a strange death.
For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, seruing the peculiar commandments that were given to them, that your children might be kept without hurt.
As namely, a cloud shadowing the campe, and where water stood before drie land appeared, and out of the red Sea a way without impediment, and out of the violent streame a greene field:
Where-thorough all the people went that were defended with your hand, seeing your marueilous strange wonders.
For they went at large like horses, and leaped like lambes, praising you O Lord, who had deliuered them.

For they were yet mindefull of the things that were done while they soiourned in the strange land, how the ground brought forth flies in stead of cattell, and how the riuer cast up a multitude of frogs in stead of fishes.
But afterwards they saw a new generation of foules, when being led with their appetite they asked delicate foods.
For quailes came up to them from the Sea, for their contentment.

And punishments came upon the sinners not without former signes by the force of thunders: for they suffered justly, according to their own wickednesse, insomuch as they used a more hard and hatefull behauiour towards strangers:
For the Sodomits did not receive those whom they knew not when they came: but these brought friends into bondage, that had well deserved of them.
And not only so: but peraduenture some respect shall be had of those, because they used strangers not friendly.
But these very grieuously afflicted them, whom they had received with feastings, and were already made partakers of the same lawes with them.

Therefore even with blindnesse were these stricken, as those were at the doores of the righteous man: when being compassed about with horrible great darknesse, every one sought the passage of his own doores.

For the elements were changed in themselues by a kind of harmonie, like as in a Psaltery notes change the name of the tune, and yet are always sounds, which may well be perceiued by the sight of the things that have been done.
For earthly things were turned into watry, and the things that before swamme in the water, now went upon the ground.
The fire had power in the water, forgetting his own vertue: and the water forgat his own quenching nature.
On the other side, the flames wasted not the flesh of the corruptible living things, though they walked therin, neither melted they the ycie kind of heauenly food, that was of nature apt to melt.
For in all things, O Lord, you did magnifie your people, and glorifie them, neither did you lightly regard them: but did assist them in every time and place.
All wisdom comes from the Lord, and is with him for ever.
Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of raine, and the days of eternity?
Who can find out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the deepe, and wisdom?
Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting.
The word of Alahayam most high, is the fountaine of wisdome, and her ways are everlasting commandments.
To whom has the root of wisdome been revealed? or who has known her wise counsels?
There is one wise and greatly to be feared; the Lord sitting upon his Throne.
He created her, and saw her, and numbred her, and powred her out upon all his workes.
She with all flesh according to his gift, and he has given her to them that love him.
The fear of the Lord is honor, and glory, and gladnesse, and a crowne of reioycing.
The fear of the Lord makes a merrie heart, and gives ioy and gladnesse, and a long life.
Who so fears the Lord, it shall go well with him at the last, and he shall find favor in the day of his death.
To fear the Lord, is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithfull in the wombe.
She has built an everlasting foundation with men, and she shall continue with their seede.
To fear the Lord, is fulnesse of wisdom, and fills men with her fruits.
She fills all their house with things desireable, and the garners with her increase.
The fear of the Lord is a crowne of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish, both which are the gifts of Alahayam: and it enlarges their reioycing that love him.
Wisdom rains downe skill and knowledge of understanding, and exalts them to honor that holde her fast.
The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and the branches thereof are long life.
The fear of the Lord drives away sins: and where it is present, it turns away wrath.
A furious man cannot be iustified, for the sway of his fury shalbe his destruction.
A patient man will beare for a time, and afterward ioy shall spring up to him.
He will hide his words for a time, and the lippes of many shall declare his wisdom.
The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisdom: but godlines is an abomination to a sinner.
If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord shall give her to you.
For the fear of the Lord is wisdome, and instruction: and faith and meekenesse are his delight.
Distrust not the fear of the Lord when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.
Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heede what you speak.

Exalt not your selfe, lest you fall, and bring dishonor upon your soul, and so Alahayam discouer your secrets, and cast you downe in the midst of the congregation, because you camest not in truth, to the fear of the Lord: but your heart is full of deceit.
My son, if you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for temptation.
Set your heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.
Cleaue to him, and depart not away, that you may be increased at your last end.
Whatever is brought upon you, take cheerefully, and be patient when you are changed to a lowe estate.
For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of aduersitie.
Believe in him, and he will helpe you, order your way aright, and trust in him.
You that fear the Lord, waite for his mercy, and go not aside, lest you fall.
You that fear the Lord, believe him, and your reward shall not faile.
You that fear the Lord, hope for good, and for everlasting ioy and mercy.
Look at the generations of old, and see, did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?
For the Lord is full of compassion, and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitifull, and forgives sins, and saueth in time of affliction.
Woe be to fearefull hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goes two ways.
Woe to him that is faint hearted, for he believes not, therefore shall he not be defended.
Woe to you that have lost patience: and what will you do when the Lord shall visite you?
They that fear the Lord, will not disobey his word, and they that love him, will keep his ways.
They that fear the Lord, will seeke that which is well pleasing to him, and they that love him, shall be filled with the Law.
They that fear the Lord, will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight:
Saying, We will fal into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men: for as his maiestie is, so is his mercy.
Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.
For the Lord has given the father honor over the children, and has confirmed the authoritie of the mother over the sons.
Who so honors his father, makes an atonement for his sins.
And he that honors his mother, is as one that layeth up treasure.
Who so honors his father, shall have ioy of his own children, and when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.
He that honors his father, shall have a long life, and he that is obedient to the Lord, shall be a comfort to his mother.
He that fears the Lord, will honor his father, and will do seruice to his parents, as to his masters.
Honor your father and mother, both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.
For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children, but the curse of the mother roots out foundations.
Glory not in the dishonour of your father, for your fathers dishonour is no glory to you.
For the glory of a man, is from the honor of his father, and a mother in dishonour, is a reproch to the children.
My son, helpe your father in his age, and grieue him not as long as he lives.
And if his understanding faile, have patience with him, and despise him not, when you are in your ful strength.
For the relieuing of your father shall not be forgotten: and in stead of sins it shall be added to build you up.
In the day of your affliction it shall be remembred, your sins also shall melt away, as the yce in the faire warme weather.
He that forsakes his father, is as a blasphemer, and he that angers his mother, is cursed of Alahayam.
My son, go on with your businesse in meekenesse, so shall you be beloued of him that is approued.
The greater you are, the more humble your selfe, and you shall find favor before the Lord.
Many are in high place and of renowne: but mysteries are reueiled to the meeke.
For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honored of the lowly.
Seeke not out the things that are too hard for you, neither search the things that are above your strength.
But what is commanded you, thinke thereupon with reuerence, for it is not needfull for you, to see with your eyes, the things that are in secret.
Be not curious in vnnecessarie matters: for moe things are showed to you, then men understand.
For many are deceiued by their own vaine opinion, and an evil suspition has ouerthrowen their judgment.
Without eyes you shall want light: professe not the knowledge therfore that you have not.
A stubborne heart shall fare evil at the last, and he that loves danger shall perish therein.
An obstinate heart shall be laden with sorrowes, and the wicked man shall heape sin upon sin.
In the punishment of the proud there is no remedie: for the plant of wickednesse has taken roote in him.
The heart of the prudent will understand a parable, and an attentiue eare is the desire of a wise man.
Water will quench a flaming fire, and alms makes an attonement for sins.
And he that repays good turnes, is mindfull of that which may come heereafter: and when he falls he shall find a stay.
My son, defraude not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eies to waite long.
Make not an hungry soul sorrowfull, neither prouoke a man in his distresse.
Adde not more trouble to an heart that is vexed, and deferre not to give to him that is in neede.
Reiect not the supplication of the afflicted, neither turne away your face from a poor man.
Turne not away your eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse you:
For if he curse you in the bitternesse of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him.
Get your selfe the love of the congregation, and bow your head to a great man.
Let it not grieue you to bowe downe your eare to the poor, and give him a friendly answer with meekenesse.
Deliuer him that suffers wrong, from the hand of the oppressour, and be not faint hearted when you sit in judgment.
Be as a father to the fatherlesse, and in stead of a husband to their mother, so shall you be as the son of the most high, and he shall love you more then your mother does.
Wisdom exalts her children, and layeth hold of them that seeke her.
He that loves her, loves life, and they that seeke to her earely, shall be filled with ioy.
He that holds her fast shall inherit glory, and wheresoeuer she enters, the Lord will blesse.
They that serve her shall minister to the Holy one, and them that love her, the Lord does love.
Who so gives eare to her, shall judge the nations, and he that attends to her, shall dwell securely.
If a man commit himselfe to her, he shall inherite her, and his generation shall hold her in possession.
For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her Lawes.
Then will she returne the straight way to him, and comfort him, and show him her secrets.
But if he go wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruine.
Obserue the opportunitie, and beware of evil, and be not ashamed when it concerns your soul.
For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame which is glory and grace.
Accept no person against your soul, and let not the reuerence of any man cause you to fall:
And refraine not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not your wisdom in her beautie.
For by speech wisdom shall be known, and learning by the word of the tongue.
In no wise speak against the truth, but be abashed of the errour of your ignorance.
Be not ashamed to confesse your sins, and force not the course of the riuer.
Make not your selfe an vnderling to a foolish man, neither accept the person of the mighty.
Striue for the truth to death, and the Lord shall fight for you.
Be not hastie in your tongue, and in your deeds slacke and remisse.
Be not as a Lion in your house, nor franticke among your servants.
Let not your hand be stretched out to receive, and shut when you should repay.
Set not your heart upon your goods, and say not, I have ynough for my life.
Folow not your own minde, and your strength, to walk in the ways of your heart:
And say not, Who shall controll me for my workes? for the Lord will surely reuenge your pride.
Say not, I have sinned, and what harme has happened to me? for the Lord is long suffering, he will in no wise let you go.
Concerning propitiation, be not without fear to adde sin to sin.
And say not, His mercy is great, he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation rests upon sinners.

Make no tarying to turne to the Lord, and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of the Lord come foorth, and in your securitie you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.
Set not your heart upon goods vniustly gotten: for they shall not profit you in the day of calamitie.
Winnow not with every winde, and go not into every way: for so does the sinner that has a double tongue.
Be stedfast in your understanding, and let your word be the same.
Be swift to hear, and let your life be sincere, and with patience give answer.
If you have understanding, answer your neighbour, if not, lay your hand upon your mouth.
Honor and shame is in talke; and the tongue of man is his fall.
Be not called a whisperer, and lye not in wait with your tongue: for a foule shame is upon the thiefe, and an evil condemnation upon the double tongue.
Be not ignorant of any thing, in a great matter or a small.
In stead of a friend, become not an enemie; for you shall inherite an ill name, shame, and reproch: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.
Extoll not your selfe in the counsel of your own heart, that your soul be not torne in pieces as a bull
You shall eat up your leaues, and loose your fruit, and leave your selfe as a dry tree.
A wicked soul shall destroy him that has it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorne of his enemies.
Sweet language will multiply friends: and a faire speaking tongue will increase kinde greetings.
Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counseller of a thousand.
If you wouldst get a friend, proue him first, and be not hasty to credit him.
For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble.
And there is a friend, who being turned to enmitie, and strife, will discouer your reproch.
Again some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of your affliction.
But in your prosperitie he will be as your selfe, and will be bould over your servants.
If you be brought low, he will be against you, and will hide himselfe from your face.
Separate your selfe from your enemies, and take heed of your friends.
A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one, has found a treasure.
Nothing does counteruaile a faithful friend, and his excellencie is vnualuable.
A faithfull friend is the medicine of life, and they that fear the Lord shall find him.
Who so fears the Lord shall direct his friendship aright, for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.
My son, gather instruction from your youth up: so shall you find wisdom until your old age.
Come to her as one that plows, and soweth, and wait for her good fruits, for you shall not toile much in labouring about her, but you shall eat of her fruits right soone.
She is very vnpleasant to the vnlearned: he that is without understanding, will not remain with her.
She will lye upon him as a mighty stone of triall, and he will cast her from him ere it be long.
For wisdom is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many.
Give eare, my son, receive my aduice, and refuse not my counsel,
And put your feet into her fetters, and your necke into her chaine.
Bow downe your shoulder, and beare her, and be not grieved with her bonds.
Come to her with your whole heart, and keep her ways with all your power.
Search and seeke, and she shall be made known to you, and when you have got hold of her, let her not go.
For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shalbe turned to your ioy.
Then shall her fetters be a strong defence for you, and her chaines a robe of glory.
For there is a golden ornament upon her, and her bandes are purple lace.
You shall put her on as a robe of honor: and shall put her about you as a crowne of ioy.
My son, if you will, you shall be taught: and if you will apply your minde, you shall be prudent.
If you love to hear, you shall receive understanding: and if you bow your eare, you shall be wise.
Stand in the multitude of the elders, and cleaue to him that is wise.
Be willing to hear every godly discourse, and let not the parables of understanding escape you.
And if you seest a man of understanding, get you betimes to him, and let your foote weare the steps of his doore.
Let your minde be upon the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish your heart, and give you wisdom at your own desire.
Do no evil, so shall no harme come to you.
Depart from the vniust, and iniquitie shall turne away from you.
My son, sow not upon the furrowes of vnrighteousnesse, and you shall not reape them seven folde.
Seeke not of the Lord preheminence, neither of the King the seate of honor.
Iustifie not your selfe before the Lord, and boast not of your wisdom before the king.
Seeke not to be judge, being not able to take away iniquitie, lest at any time you fear the person of the mighty, and lay a stumbling blocke in the way of your vprightnesse.
Offend not against the multitude of a city, and then you shall not cast your selfe downe among the people.
Bind not one sin upon another, for in one you shall not be vnpunished.
Say not, Alahayam will look upon the multitude of my oblations, and when I offer to the most High Alahayam, he will accept it.
Be not faint hearted when you makest your prayer, and neglect not to give alms.
Laugh no man to scorne in the bitternesse of his soul: for there is one which humbles and exalts.
Deuise not a lie against your brother: neither do the like to your friend.
Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custome thereof is not good.
Use not many words in a multitude of Elders, and make not much babling when you pray.
Hate not laborious worke, neither husbandrie, which the most High has ordained.
Number not your selfe among the multitude of sinners, but remember that wrath will not tary long.
Humble your soul greatly: for the vengeance of the ungodly is fire and wormes.
Change not a friend for any good by no meanes: neither a faithfull brother for the gold of Ophir.
Forgoe not a wise and good woman: for her grace is above gold.
Whereas your servant works truely, entreate him not evil, nor the hireling that bestows himselfe wholly for you.
Let your soul love a good servant, and defraud him not of liberty.
Have you cattell? have an eye to them, and if they be for your profit, keep them with you.
Have you children? instruct them, and bow downe their necke from their youth.
Have you daughters? have care of their body, and shewe not your selfe cheerefull toward them.
Marrie your daughter, and so shall you have performed a weightie matter: but give her to a man of understanding.
Have you a wife after your minde? forsake her not, but give not your selfe over to a light woman.
Honor your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrowes of your mother.
Remember that you were begot of them, and how canst you recompense them the things that they have done for you?
Fear the Lord with all your soul, and reuerence his priests.
Love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.

Fear the Lord, and honor the priest: and give him his portion, as it is commanded you, the first fruits, and the trespasse offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of the holy things.
And stretch your hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected
A gift has grace in the sight of every man living, and for the dead deteine it not.
Faile not to be with them that weepe, and mourne with them that mourne.
Be not slow to visit the sicke: for that shall make you to be beloued.
Whatever you takest in hand, remember the end, and you shall never do amisse.
Striue not with a mighty man, lest you fall into his hands.
Be not at variance with a rich man, lest he ouerweigh you: for gold has destroyed many, and peruerted the hearts of kings.
Striue not with a man that is full of tongue, and heape not wood upon his fire.
Iest not with a rude man, lest your ancestours be disgraced.
Reproch not a man that turns from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
Dishonour not a man in his old age: for even some of us waxe old.
Reioice not over your greatest enemie being dead, but remember that we die all.
Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint your selfe with their prouerbs; for of them you shall learne instruction, and how to serve great men with ease.
Misse not the discourse of the Elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them you shall learne understanding, and to give answer as need requires.
Kindle not the coales of a sinner, lest you be burnt with the flame of his fire.
